chunks.text: Customer Support Escalation Procedures Owning area: Customer_support Last reviewed: August 2026 Document ID: CS-POL-014 Version: 3.2 Applies to: IronStore customer support operations across Europe 1. Purpose and Overview This procedure defines how IronStore identifies, manages, and escalates customer contacts that cannot be resolved through standard frontline support. It is intended to ensure consistent decisions, timely ownership, and appropriate protection of customer, payment, product, and company information. Escalation is required when a case involves material customer impact, operational risk, legal or regulatory considerations, reputational risk, or a resolution outside the agent’s authority. Escalation does not remove ownership from the original agent unless a receiving team formally accepts the case. The procedure applies to contacts received through email, telephone, chat, social media, marketplace messaging, and the IronStore Help Centre. 2. Scope This procedure covers:  Order, delivery, return, refund, payment, and product-support cases.  Complaints involving vulnerable customers, discrimination, safety, or accessibility.  Suspected fraud, account compromise, payment abuse, or privacy incidents.  Product safety concerns, recalls, counterfeit allegations, and regulatory requests.  High-value, high-volume, or executive-level complaints.  Escalations between Customer Support, Logistics, Payments, Trust & Safety, Legal, and Product teams. This procedure does not replace:  The Personal Data Incident Response Plan.  The Product Safety and Recall Standard.  The Chargeback Handling Guide.  Country-specific requirements approved by Legal or Compliance.
The Chargeback Handling Guide.  Country-specific requirements approved by Legal or Compliance.

3. Policy Statement IronStore support cases must be resolved at the lowest appropriate level, using approved tools and decision limits. Escalations must be based on documented facts rather than customer status, personal preference, or pressure from a third party. Agents must:  Record all material facts in Zendesk before escalating.  Use the correct escalation category and priority.  Avoid promising an outcome that requires another team’s approval.  Provide the customer with a realistic next-update time.  Protect personal data by using approved internal systems only.  Continue monitoring the case until ownership is accepted or resolution is confirmed. No employee may disclose internal investigation details, fraud rules, warehouse controls, security information, or another customer’s data. 4. Standard Escalation Procedure 4.1 Initial assessment The assigned agent must complete the following checks: 1. Confirm the customer’s identity using the approved verification steps. 2. Review the full contact history, order record, payment status, and delivery events. 3. Check for duplicate tickets, open complaints, chargebacks, or previous escalations. 4. Identify the customer’s country, applicable language, currency, and service terms. 5. Determine whether the case is routine, priority, urgent, or critical. 6. Record the reason for escalation in Zendesk using the relevant macro. If information is missing, the agent should request it before escalating unless delay could increase customer or business risk. 4.2 Escalation record requirements Every escalation must include:  Order number, customer ID, and relevant ticket links.  A short factual summary of the issue.  Actions already taken and their

escalating unless delay could increase customer or business risk. 4.2 Escalation record requirements Every escalation must include:  Order number, customer ID, and relevant ticket links.  A short factual summary of the issue.  Actions already taken and their outcomes.

 The requested decision or assistance.  Applicable deadline or customer commitment.  Financial value, if relevant.  Screenshots, carrier events, payment references, or other evidence.  Any known legal, safety, media, or executive involvement. Do not copy full payment card numbers, passwords, identity documents, or unnecessary personal information into ticket notes. 4.3 Priority levels | Priority | Use when | Acknowledge | Target first action | |---|---|---:|---:| | P1 – Critical | Safety risk, active data-security concern, major outage, or widespread customer impact | 15 minutes | 1 hour | | P2 – Urgent | Significant financial loss, vulnerable customer risk, executive complaint, or likely regulatory breach | 1 hour | 4 hours | | P3 – High | Repeated failed resolution, high-value order, serious delivery or payment dispute | 4 business hours | 1 business day | | P4 – Standard | Specialist review required without immediate material risk | 1 business day | 3 business days | Service targets apply during the receiving team’s operating hours. P1 and P2 cases are monitored outside normal hours through the on-call rota. 5. Escalation Categories and Routing 5.1 Order, delivery, and warehouse issues Escalate to Logistics Operations when:  A parcel is missing after the carrier investigation window.  Tracking shows delivery, but the customer disputes receipt.  A shipment is held by customs or repeatedly misrouted.  A warehouse error affects multiple orders or a promised delivery date.  A replacement cannot be issued through the standard workflow. The

shows delivery, but the customer disputes receipt.  A shipment is held by customs or repeatedly misrouted.  A warehouse error affects multiple orders or a promised delivery date.  A replacement cannot be issued through the standard workflow. The agent must include the carrier, tracking number, delivery address at country and city level, last scan, and promised resolution date. Address details must not be repeated in unprotected email or external chat. Orders above €500, or orders with more than two failed delivery attempts, require a P3 escalation unless a P1 or P2 condition applies.

5.2 Refunds, payments, and chargebacks Escalate to Payments Operations when:  A refund is overdue by more than five business days after approval.  The payment was captured but the order was cancelled.  A duplicate charge is confirmed or reasonably suspected.  A chargeback notice is received.  The payment provider reports a technical or compliance hold. Agents may approve refunds only within their role limit and the Refund Authority Matrix CS-FIN-006. Refunds above €250, goodwill credits above €75, or exceptions to published return terms require Team Lead approval. Amounts above €1,000 require Payments Operations approval and Finance notification. Do not advise a customer to withdraw a chargeback before the case has been reviewed by Payments Operations. 5.3 Fraud and account security Escalate immediately to Trust & Safety when there is evidence of:  Account takeover or unauthorised password or email changes.  Unrecognised orders, payment methods, or delivery addresses.  Multiple accounts using suspicious vouchers or referral credits.  Resale, bot activity, coupon abuse, or organised returns fraud.  Threats to expose customer or employee information. Use the Fraud Escalation form in Zendesk. Do not accuse the customer of fraud or disclose detection criteria. Apply an account security hold only when authorised by Trust & Safety or under the documented emergency playbook. Suspected personal data breaches must also be reported through Security Hub within 30 minutes. Customer Support must not independently investigate or delete evidence. 5.4 Product safety and quality Escalate to Product Compliance as P1 or P2

the documented emergency playbook. Suspected personal data breaches must also be reported through Security Hub within 30 minutes. Customer Support must not independently investigate or delete evidence. 5.4 Product safety and quality Escalate to Product Compliance as P1 or P2 when a customer reports:  Fire, smoke, electric shock, explosion, serious injury, or hospitalisation.  A product defect that could cause injury or property damage.  Suspected counterfeit, unsafe, or incorrectly labelled goods.  A possible recall or repeated safety issue involving the same product. Capture the product name, SKU, batch or serial number, purchase date, customer description, and photographs if voluntarily provided. Tell the customer to stop using the product when appropriate, without diagnosing the fault. Do not provide technical repair instructions unless approved by Product Compliance.

5.5 Complaints, legal, and regulatory matters Escalate to Customer Advocacy when:  The customer has made two unsuccessful contacts about the same issue.  The customer alleges discrimination, harassment, or unreasonable treatment.  A formal complaint is requested.  The customer references a regulator, court, solicitor, journalist, or elected representative.  The requested remedy exceeds normal policy and may create a precedent. Route formal legal notices, data-subject rights concerns, consumer authority requests, and threats of litigation to Legal & Compliance. Use the customer’s country queue and preserve the original wording. Do not interpret legislation or commit to a legal position. Complaints involving a vulnerable customer, self-harm reference, or immediate personal danger must be escalated to the Duty Manager. Emergency services should be contacted only where policy and local law permit, or where there is an immediate and credible threat. 5.6 Public and executive complaints Social media cases should be moved to a private channel without requesting public disclosure of order details. Escalate to Customer Advocacy if the post alleges safety, discrimination, privacy loss, widespread failure, or employee misconduct. Cases involving the CEO, executive leadership, investor relations, a government office, or a recognised media organisation must be tagged Executive Review. The agent should acknowledge receipt, avoid speculation, and provide the approved next-update time. 6. Handover, Communication, and Closure The receiving team must accept or reject an escalation in Zendesk within the applicable acknowledgement target. A rejection must state the missing information or correct destination. The original agent remains the customer-facing owner

next-update time. 6. Handover, Communication, and Closure The receiving team must accept or reject an escalation in Zendesk within the applicable acknowledgement target. A rejection must state the missing information or correct destination. The original agent remains the customer-facing owner unless:  The receiving team assigns a named case owner.  The Duty Manager transfers ownership.  Legal, Security, or Trust & Safety requires restricted communication. Customer updates must be sent at least:  Every one business day for P1 and P2 cases.  Every two business days for P3 cases.  At each agreed milestone for P4 cases.

If no new information is available, the update should state that the investigation remains open and provide the next review date. Never use “resolved” merely because an escalation was submitted. A case may be closed when the approved action is complete, the customer has been informed, and all internal notes and evidence are recorded. P1 and P2 cases require a closure note identifying root cause, customer impact, corrective action, and any follow-up owner. 7. Roles and Responsibilities  Support Agent: Verify, document, classify, escalate, and maintain customer communication.  Team Lead: Approve exceptions within authority, review P2/P3 cases, and support difficult contacts.  Duty Manager: Own P1 incidents, out-of-hours decisions, and cross-functional coordination.  Customer Advocacy: Manage formal complaints, executive contacts, and repeated service failures.  Payments Operations: Review payment exceptions, refunds, chargebacks, and financial controls.  Trust & Safety: Investigate fraud, account compromise, abuse, and suspicious activity.  Product Compliance: Assess product safety, recalls, and regulatory product concerns.  Legal & Compliance: Advise on legal notices, regulatory matters, privacy rights, and precedent-setting remedies.  Knowledge Management: Maintain macros, decision trees, and quarterly procedure reviews. 8. Customer Support Knowledge Base Style Guide Owning area: Customer_support Last reviewed: August 2026 Document ID: CS-KB-STD-004 Policy owner: Head of Customer Support Operations 1. Purpose and Overview This guide defines how IronStore customer support knowledge base (KB) articles are written, reviewed, published, and maintained. It applies to customer-facing Help Centre content and internal agent guidance used across European markets. The objective is to provide accurate, easy-to-scan instructions that help customers resolve common issues without contacting support. Articles must reflect current IronStore processes, product categories, delivery options, payment methods, and country-specific requirements. The KB is maintained in GuideHub, with operational links to Zendesk, OrderSphere, ReturnFlow, and the IronStore Product Catalogue (IPC). GuideHub is the authoritative source for approved support content. 2. Scope This standard applies to:  Public Help Centre articles, troubleshooting guides, FAQs, and policy explanations.  Internal agent procedures, saved replies, escalation notes, and workflow instructions.  Content created for all supported European storefronts and languages.  New articles, major revisions, translations, and republished content.  Content owners, subject-matter experts, translators, quality reviewers, and support agents. This standard does not replace legal, privacy, payment-security, product-safety, or marketplace policies. Where requirements conflict, the stricter approved policy applies. 3. Content Policy and Procedures 3.1 Article selection and ownership Create an article when a question is:  Asked regularly through Zendesk.  Likely to be solved without account-specific investigation.  Relevant to more than one product, order, or country.
when a question is:  Asked regularly through Zendesk.  Likely to be solved without account-specific investigation.  Relevant to more than one product, order, or country.

 Needed to explain a change in policy, system, or customer journey. Do not publish an article for:  A single customer’s order or account details.  Unconfirmed product information.  Temporary incidents unless marked as a service notice.  Advice that could create safety, legal, financial, or medical risk. Each article must have one named Content Owner in GuideHub. The owner is accountable for accuracy, review dates, and updates following process changes. 3.2 Article types and required structure Use one of the following article types:  How-to: Steps the customer can complete independently.  Policy: Rules for returns, refunds, delivery, payments, or accounts.  Troubleshooting: Checks and actions for a specific issue.  FAQ: Short answers to common questions.  Internal procedure: Agent-only handling and escalation instructions.  Service notice: Time-limited information about an outage or disruption. Use this order unless there is a clear reason to vary it: 1. Descriptive title. 2. One-sentence summary of the customer outcome. 3. Eligibility or important conditions. 4. Numbered steps or short answer sections. 5. Exceptions and escalation guidance. 6. Related links. 7. Review metadata for internal articles. Start with the answer. Do not open with background, apologies, or promotional language. 3.3 Titles, headings, and summaries Titles must describe the customer’s task or question. Preferred:  “How to change a delivery address”  “When will my refund be processed?”  “What to do if your parcel arrives damaged”
or question. Preferred:  “How to change a delivery address”  “When will my refund be processed?”  “What to do if your parcel arrives damaged”

Avoid:  “Important information about orders”  “We are here to help”  “Delivery FAQ and other useful information” Use sentence case for titles and headings. Keep titles below 70 characters where possible. Use headings to separate decisions or stages, not to create unnecessary visual breaks. The opening summary should be no more than two sentences and should state the main outcome, expected timeframe, or key restriction. 3.4 Writing style and tone IronStore content must be clear, neutral, practical, and respectful. Use:  “You can request a return within 30 days of delivery.”  “Enter the email address used for the order.”  “We will email you when the refund is issued.” Avoid:  Blame: “You entered the wrong address.”  Unclear promises: “Your parcel should arrive soon.”  Internal language: “The ticket has been routed to L2.”  Excessive enthusiasm, slang, or humour.  Legalistic wording where plain language is sufficient. Address the reader as you and IronStore as we. Use active voice and short sentences. Explain unavoidable terms at first use, for example, “proof of delivery (POD).” Do not use:  All-capital words for emphasis.  Multiple exclamation marks.  Emoji in policy or troubleshooting content.  “Simply,” “obviously,” “guaranteed,” or “always” unless factually exact.  Claims that a result is certain when it depends on a carrier, bank, seller, or manufacturer. 3.5 Steps, conditions, and decision points Write instructions as numbered steps. Each step should contain one action.
a result is certain when it depends on a carrier, bank, seller, or manufacturer. 3.5 Steps, conditions, and decision points Write instructions as numbered steps. Each step should contain one action.

 Begin with a verb: Open, Select, Upload, Contact.  Name the exact button or field shown in the current interface.  Put conditions before steps where they affect eligibility.  State what the customer should see after completing an action.  Include the next action if a step fails. Use bullets for lists of requirements or examples. Use tables only when they improve comparison, such as delivery methods or refund timeframes. For decision points, use clear “If / Then” wording:  If the tracking page shows “Delivered” but you cannot find the parcel, contact us within 48 hours.  If the item is damaged, do not return it before uploading photographs. Do not direct customers to internal queues, team names, or unpublished tools. 3.6 Product, order, and policy accuracy Before publication, verify all operational facts in the relevant system:  Product specifications: IPC or the manufacturer’s approved data sheet.  Order and delivery status: OrderSphere and the carrier portal.  Return eligibility: ReturnFlow and the current country policy.  Payment status: PayCore transaction record.  Promotions: current campaign brief in CampaignVault. Never copy customer-specific information into a public article. Do not publish full order numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, payment details, or screenshots containing personal data. Timeframes must include the starting point:  “Within 14 calendar days of delivery.”  “Refunds are issued within five business days after inspection.”  “Bank processing may take an additional three to seven business days.” State the applicable country or storefront when rules

the starting point:  “Within 14 calendar days of delivery.”  “Refunds are issued within five business days after inspection.”  “Bank processing may take an additional three to seven business days.” State the applicable country or storefront when rules differ. Do not use “Europe-wide” unless the Legal or Policy team has confirmed that the rule is uniform. 3.7 Returns, refunds, and delivery wording Use the approved terminology:  Return request: customer asks to send an item back.  Return label: shipping label issued by IronStore or a seller.  Refund issued: IronStore has released the funds.

 Refund received: funds are visible in the customer’s account.  Delivery estimate: expected date, not a guarantee.  Delivery guarantee: use only where contractually confirmed. For damaged, incorrect, or missing items, explain the evidence required and the response target. Standard guidance is:  Customer reports damage within 48 hours of delivery where possible.  Customer provides photographs of the item, packaging, and shipping label.  Support reviews the case within two business days.  High-value claims above €250 require Customer Resolution Team review.  Suspected fraud, repeated claims, or safety concerns go to Trust & Safety. Do not instruct customers to dispose of an item unless the case record includes an approved disposal instruction. 3.8 Accessibility and localisation All customer-facing content must meet IronStore’s accessibility baseline:  Use descriptive link text, not “click here.”  Provide meaningful alt text for essential images.  Do not use colour alone to communicate status.  Keep paragraphs to four lines or fewer on standard desktop view.  Use headings in logical order.  Avoid screenshots when text instructions are sufficient. Content is initially written in International English and translated through LinguaDesk. Localisation reviewers must check:  Currency, date, time, and measurement formats.  Country-specific consumer rights and delivery terms.  Local carrier and payment names.  Formality, terminology, and prohibited claims. Machine or vendor translation must not be published without review by an approved language reviewer. 3.9 Links, screenshots, and system references Use stable GuideHub links where available. Do not link directly

and payment names.  Formality, terminology, and prohibited claims. Machine or vendor translation must not be published without review by an approved language reviewer. 3.9 Links, screenshots, and system references Use stable GuideHub links where available. Do not link directly to temporary Zendesk views, agent dashboards, or personal documents. Screenshots must:  Show only the relevant area.

 Use the current interface.  Exclude personal data, internal IDs, and browser notifications.  Include a short caption or alt text.  Be reviewed whenever the interface changes. Broken links, outdated images, or missing translations are content defects and must be corrected within five business days of identification. 3.10 Review, approval, and publication The Content Owner completes the draft and records the source of each policy or operational claim. Required approval depends on content type:  Standard how-to or FAQ: Support Knowledge Manager.  Returns, refunds, delivery, or payment policy: Support Operations Manager and relevant Policy Owner.  Privacy or personal-data content: Privacy Counsel.  Product safety or regulated products: Product Compliance Manager.  Country-specific legal wording: Local Market Lead. The Knowledge Manager publishes approved content in GuideHub and records:  Owner and approving roles.  Applicable markets and languages.  Publication date.  Next review date.  Related systems or policy references. Standard articles are reviewed every six months. Payment, privacy, safety, and legal articles are reviewed every three months. Articles affected by a process or system change must be reviewed before the change goes live. Agents should flag inaccurate or unclear content using the “Report KB issue” form in Zendesk. Critical errors affecting refunds, safety, privacy, or customer eligibility must be escalated to the Team Lead immediately and corrected or temporarily unpublished within one business day. 4. Roles and Responsibilities  Support Knowledge Manager: Owns this standard, publishing controls, audits, and reporting.  Content Owner: Drafts, maintains, and reviews assigned articles.  Subject-Matter Expert: Confirms operational or product accuracy.  Local Market Lead: Confirms country-specific language and requirements.  Language Reviewer: Validates translated content in LinguaDesk.  Support Team Lead: Identifies agent content gaps and urgent inaccuracies.  Support Agent: Uses approved content and reports defects; does not create unapproved customer policy.

Refund & Complaint Handling Policy Owning area: Customer_support Policy ID: CS-POL-014 Version: 3.2 Last reviewed: August 2026 Approved by: Director of Customer Operations Applies to: IronStore EU operating companies and customer-support channels 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines how IronStore receives, investigates, and resolves customer complaints and refund requests. It is intended to provide consistent outcomes, protect customer rights, and ensure that cases are recorded accurately for operational and regulatory reporting. IronStore sells consumer products across Europe, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and other categories. Refund eligibility may differ by product type, fulfilment route, payment method, country, and applicable consumer law. Where local law provides a stronger customer right than this policy, the legal requirement takes precedence. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  Orders placed through IronStore websites, mobile applications, and approved marketplace channels.  Customer contacts received by email, web form, live chat, telephone, and social-care channels.  Refunds for cancelled orders, returns, damaged or faulty goods, failed delivery, duplicate charges, and service errors.  Complaints about products, delivery, payment, customer service, sellers, or fulfilment partners.  Cases handled by Customer Support, Payments Operations, Warehouse Operations, and Marketplace Support. This policy does not replace product-specific safety procedures, payment-provider rules, or country-specific legal guidance. 3. Policy Statement IronStore will:  Acknowledge complaints and refund requests promptly.  Apply the same decision rules to comparable cases.  Provide clear explanations when a request is declined or only partly approved.  Record all material actions in

3. Policy Statement IronStore will:  Acknowledge complaints and refund requests promptly.  Apply the same decision rules to comparable cases.  Provide clear explanations when a request is declined or only partly approved.  Record all material actions in the approved case-management system.

 Protect customer data and limit access to staff with a business need.  Escalate safety, legal, fraud, and executive-risk matters without delay.  Pay approved refunds to the original payment method unless an approved exception applies. Customer Support must not promise a refund before eligibility has been checked, except where a published automatic-refund rule clearly applies. 4. Standard Refund Procedure 4.1 Case intake and verification The agent must locate the order in ServiceHub, using the order number, verified email address, or approved marketplace reference. Before discussing order details or issuing a refund, the agent must verify at least two approved identifiers, such as:  Customer email address and order number.  Delivery postcode and product description.  Payment token suffix and order date. Agents must not request or record full card numbers, CVV codes, account passwords, or unnecessary identity documents. The agent records:  Contact channel and date.  Customer’s stated reason.  Affected item, quantity, and order line.  Evidence supplied, including photographs or carrier information.  Requested outcome and applicable policy reason code. 4.2 Eligibility assessment The agent checks the following in ServiceHub and OrderCore: 1. Order status and fulfilment route. 2. Delivery date or confirmed cancellation date. 3. Return-window status. 4. Product category restrictions. 5. Previous refunds, replacements, or related complaints. 6. Payment settlement status and refund capability. For standard consumer returns, the applicable country return period is shown in the customer’s order terms. Unless a longer legal or commercial period applies, unopened and resalable goods

refunds, replacements, or related complaints. 6. Payment settlement status and refund capability. For standard consumer returns, the applicable country return period is shown in the customer’s order terms. Unless a longer legal or commercial period applies, unopened and resalable goods are accepted within 30 calendar days of

delivery. Product-specific exceptions include:  Personalised goods: normally non-returnable unless faulty.  Sealed hygiene or beauty products: non-returnable after seal removal where permitted by law.  Digital content: subject to acceptance and commencement rules.  Large or hazardous goods: collection may be required.  Marketplace items: the marketplace seller’s approved return workflow applies. A faulty, damaged, incorrect, or materially misdescribed item must not be rejected solely because the standard return window has expired. The agent follows the applicable statutory remedy process and consults Returns Operations where the remedy is unclear. 4.3 Evidence and inspection Evidence should be proportionate to the issue. Agents may request:  Clear photographs of damaged packaging or product.  A short video for intermittent faults where practical.  Carrier damage details or delivery confirmation.  Serial number or batch information for controlled products. Do not request evidence that is unsafe, unreasonable, or already available in IronStore systems. For low-value items, the No-Return Refund Matrix may permit a refund without physical return. The current matrix is:  Up to €25: agent may refund or replace without approval when evidence is sufficient.  €25.01–€150: team-lead approval is required for a no-return refund unless an automatic rule applies.  Over €150: Returns Operations or Payments Operations approval is required.  Any safety-related product: immediate escalation, regardless of value. 4.4 Refund approval and processing The agent selects the correct reason code and enters the amount in ServiceHub. The system performs duplicate-refund and open-dispute checks before submission. Approval requirements:  Up

 Any safety-related product: immediate escalation, regardless of value. 4.4 Refund approval and processing The agent selects the correct reason code and enters the amount in ServiceHub. The system performs duplicate-refund and open-dispute checks before submission. Approval requirements:  Up to €150: trained agent within documented authority.  €150.01–€500: Customer Support Team Lead.  Above €500: Customer Operations Manager and Finance Operations.  Any goodwill amount above €50: Team Lead approval.  Any refund outside policy: Customer Operations Manager approval, with rationale recorded.

Refunds are normally returned to the original payment method. Finance Operations handles exceptions such as expired cards, closed accounts, cash-on-delivery payments, or payment-provider limitations. Expected processing times after approval:  Card and digital wallet refunds: usually 3–7 business days.  Bank-transfer refunds: usually 3–5 business days after bank details are validated.  Marketplace refunds: according to the marketplace settlement timetable.  Refunds awaiting warehouse inspection: decision within five business days of receipt unless a specialist assessment is required. The customer must receive a confirmation showing the approved amount, refund method, and expected processing time. 4.5 Partial refunds, replacements, and goodwill A partial refund may be offered where the customer keeps an item with a minor, documented defect and the solution is lawful and commercially appropriate. The amount must reflect the issue and must not be used to avoid a statutory remedy. Replacement is preferred when:  The item is unavailable for immediate refund processing.  The customer requests a replacement and stock is available.  Replacement is operationally safer or faster than repair. Goodwill credits are discretionary and must not be described as a legal entitlement. Agents must not issue goodwill to close a complaint involving safety, discrimination, suspected fraud, or a serious data incident; those cases require escalation. 5. Complaint Handling Procedure 5.1 Definition and acknowledgement A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction that requires a response, investigation, or corrective action. The agent creates a Complaint case in ServiceHub rather than treating it only as a standard enquiry. The

Complaint Handling Procedure 5.1 Definition and acknowledgement A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction that requires a response, investigation, or corrective action. The agent creates a Complaint case in ServiceHub rather than treating it only as a standard enquiry. The acknowledgement should include:  Complaint reference number.  Summary of the issue as understood.  Named owner or responsible team.  Expected next update date.  Any information still required from the customer. Target timeframes:

 Acknowledge within one business day.  Provide a substantive response within five business days.  Resolve standard complaints within ten business days where practical.  Notify the customer if an investigation will take longer and provide a revised date. 5.2 Investigation and resolution The case owner reviews order history, contact notes, warehouse scans, carrier events, payment records, and relevant seller communications. Staff must avoid speculative statements and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions. Possible outcomes include:  Explanation with no further action.  Refund, replacement, repair, or return arrangement.  Delivery investigation with the carrier or fulfilment centre.  Product or seller escalation.  Process correction and customer apology.  Formal referral to Legal, Compliance, or Product Safety. The final response must be clear, respectful, and specific. It should state:  What was reviewed.  The decision and reason.  Any refund or corrective action.  Expected completion date.  How the customer may request a review. 5.3 Escalation triggers Immediate escalation through the Risk & Escalations queue is required for:  Injury, fire, electric shock, contamination, or suspected product safety risk.  Allegations of discrimination, harassment, or abusive staff conduct.  Threats of legal action, regulator contact, media exposure, or executive complaint.  Suspected payment fraud, account takeover, or organised refund abuse.  Repeated delivery failures affecting multiple customers.  Requests from law enforcement, regulators, or data-protection authorities.  Vulnerable-customer concerns requiring specialist support. Product Safety cases must also be logged in IncidentTrack within four hours. Staff must not

organised refund abuse.  Repeated delivery failures affecting multiple customers.  Requests from law enforcement, regulators, or data-protection authorities.  Vulnerable-customer concerns requiring specialist support. Product Safety cases must also be logged in IncidentTrack within four hours. Staff must not advise customers to continue using a potentially unsafe product.

5.4 Review and deadlock If a customer disputes the outcome, the case is reassigned to a Team Lead or Complaints Specialist who was not the original decision-maker where possible. The review should be completed within five business days. A second review may change the outcome only when new evidence, a policy error, or an exceptional circumstance is identified. Repeated contacts about the same resolved matter may be managed under the Reasonable Contact Standard, but genuine new information must always be assessed. 6. Fraud, Abuse, and Chargebacks Refund abuse indicators may include repeated claims of non-delivery, inconsistent damage evidence, serial-number mismatches, or multiple accounts linked to the same payment instrument. Agents must not accuse customers or disclose fraud-detection rules. Suspected abuse is referred to Trust & Payments using the reason code REFUND-RISK. Legitimate customer cases must continue to receive a timely response while checks are performed. When a card chargeback is received:  Payments Operations owns the dispute response.  Customer Support must not issue a duplicate refund without approval.  Relevant delivery, refund, and communication evidence must be preserved.  The case outcome must be linked to the original ServiceHub record. 7. Records, Reporting, and Data Retention All decisions, approvals, customer communications, and evidence references must be stored in ServiceHub. Attachments containing sensitive information must use the restricted evidence repository, not personal drives or email inboxes. Customer data is handled according to the Privacy and Records Retention Standard. Staff must not export case lists unless approved for a defined operational

Attachments containing sensitive information must use the restricted evidence repository, not personal drives or email inboxes. Customer data is handled according to the Privacy and Records Retention Standard. Staff must not export case lists unless approved for a defined operational purpose. Returns & Reverse Logistics Procedure Owning area: Deliveries Last reviewed: August 2026 Document ID: DEL-RET-004 Version: 3.2 Applies to: IronStore EU operations 1. Purpose and Overview This procedure defines how IronStore receives, assesses, refunds, replaces, repairs, and disposes of returned products. It covers customer-initiated returns, carrier exceptions, failed deliveries, warehouse errors, and products rejected during quality control. The objective is to provide a consistent customer experience while controlling reverse-logistics cost, protecting resale value, and ensuring compliance with applicable European consumer, product-safety, environmental, and data-protection requirements. All returns must be traceable from the original order through final disposition. The official record is maintained in ReturnFlow, integrated with ShopCore, WMS Atlas, carrier portals, and the finance platform LedgerOne. 2. Scope This procedure applies to:  Customer returns from EU and EEA delivery destinations.  Products fulfilled from IronStore warehouses in Germany, Poland, and the Netherlands.  Items returned through parcel carriers, pickup services, partner drop-off points, or warehouse collections.  Refunds, exchanges, replacements, repairs, partial refunds, and store-credit decisions.  Products classified as resaleable, open-box, damaged, defective, unsafe, incomplete, or unsellable. This procedure does not replace:  The Product Safety Incident Procedure (QMS-PS-002).  The Personal Data Handling Standard (SEC-DATA-006).  Marketplace-specific return rules where those rules are contractually stricter.  Supplier warranty or manufacturer repair procedures. 3. Policy Statement IronStore accepts eligible consumer returns in line with statutory withdrawal rights and the applicable product-category terms shown at checkout. charged an unauthorized return fee. Returns must be processed fairly and consistently. The standard operational targets are:  Return request acknowledged within one business day.  Return label or drop-off instructions issued within one business day of approval.  Warehouse receipt scan completed within 24 hours of physical receipt.  Initial inspection completed within two business days of receipt.  Refund released within one business day after approval.  Customer cases older than seven calendar days without a decision escalated to the Returns Team Lead. 4. The case must include:  Order number, customer ID, SKU, quantity, and reason code.  Purchase channel and delivery country.  Photos or supporting evidence where damage, defect, or incorrect item is reported.  Requested resolution: refund, replacement, exchange, repair, or credit. The system checks:  Whether the item belongs to the order.  Whether the request is within the applicable return period.  Whether the category has special restrictions.  Whether a previous refund, replacement, or claim exists.  Whether the item is subject to a safety, hygiene, or regulatory block. Examples of restricted products include opened cosmetics, personal-care items with a broken hygiene seal, software with an activated license, customized goods, and products legally restricted from resale after use. Examples of restricted products include opened cosmetics, personal-care items with a broken hygiene seal, software with an activated license, customized goods, and products legally restricted from resale after use. Customer Service must not promise an exception without approval from the Returns Team Lead. For approved returns, ReturnFlow generates a return authorization number (RMA) and the appropriate carrier label. The RMA is valid for 14 calendar days unless a different period is shown in the case. 4.2 Return Routing and Carrier Handover Return routing is determined by product dimensions, value, hazard classification, and warehouse capacity.  Standard parcels use the contracted DHL Parcel Return or DPD Return service.

 Oversized items use Rhenus Home Logistics or the original delivery partner.  Lithium-battery products must follow the Dangerous Goods Matrix DEL-DG-011.  High-value items above €500 require tracked service and an RMA-linked label.  Items above €1,000 require signature at handover and enhanced receipt verification. Customers must not return products to a warehouse address manually provided by an employee. The label generated in ReturnFlow ensures correct routing and cost allocation. When a carrier reports a failed collection, the case is rescheduled once automatically. A second failure is assigned to Customer Service for customer contact and alternative routing. 4.3 Warehouse Receipt The receiving operative scans the parcel barcode and RMA into WMS Atlas. If the label is unreadable, the operative searches by order number or carrier tracking number and creates an exception record. At receipt, the operative must: 1. Photograph visibly damaged outer packaging. 2. Record parcel weight where the item is high-value, incomplete, or disputed. 3. Confirm the SKU and quantity. 4. Place the item in the correct inspection lane. 5. Update ReturnFlow with receipt date, warehouse, and condition of packaging. Unidentified parcels are placed in the Returns Reconciliation Cage. The Returns Control Specialist investigates within three business days using carrier data, order records, and customer contact details available in the system. Unresolved parcels are escalated to the Logistics Operations Manager after ten business days. 4.4 Inspection and Condition Grading The inspection associate follows the applicable category checklist in WMS Atlas. The inspection must verify:  Product identity and

in the system. Unresolved parcels are escalated to the Logistics Operations Manager after ten business days. 4.4 Inspection and Condition Grading The inspection associate follows the applicable category checklist in WMS Atlas. The inspection must verify:  Product identity and serial number, where applicable.  Functional operation using the approved test.  Completeness of accessories, manuals, cables, and packaging.  Signs of use, damage, contamination, or tampering.  Safety concerns, recalled-batch indicators, and counterfeit risk.  Customer-reported fault compared with observed condition. The associate records findings and photographs for:  Electronics and appliances above €250.  Any item marked damaged, defective, incomplete, or counterfeit suspected.  Any customer dispute involving condition or missing parts.

Condition grades are:  A – New/resalable: Unused or indistinguishable from new, complete, and correctly packaged.  B – Open-box: Functional, minor packaging impact, no material product damage.  C – Used or cosmetically marked: Functional but not suitable for standard new inventory.  D – Defective or incomplete: Requires repair, parts replacement, supplier review, or controlled liquidation.  E – Unsafe or prohibited: Must be quarantined and prevented from resale. Grade A items are returned to available stock only after the inventory controller confirms the SKU and quantity. Grade B and C items are transferred to the approved outlet or refurbishment inventory pools. Grade D items are routed according to the disposition decision. Grade E items remain in the locked quarantine area. 4.5 Resolution and Refund The inspection result triggers a recommended resolution in ReturnFlow. The following approval limits apply:  Up to €250: Returns Team Lead may approve refund, replacement, or partial refund.  €250–€1,000: Returns Team Lead approval plus Finance Operations review for non-standard outcomes.  Above €1,000: Deliveries Manager and Finance Operations approval.  Any safety, fraud, counterfeit, or legal issue: mandatory Compliance referral. Refunds are normally issued to the original payment method through LedgerOne. Refund amount includes the eligible product price and standard outbound delivery charge where required by the applicable withdrawal rules. Additional delivery upgrades are not automatically refundable. A refund may be reduced only when permitted by law and supported by evidence of customer-caused diminished value. The decision and evidence must be recorded

A refund may be reduced only when permitted by law and supported by evidence of customer-caused diminished value. The decision and evidence must be recorded before the refund is released. Replacement orders must be created from the original case, not as an unrelated manual order. The replacement SKU, warehouse, expected dispatch date, and any price difference must be recorded. 4.6 Exceptions, Fraud, and Disputes Potential fraud indicators include repeated high-value returns, serial-number mismatch, empty parcels, altered labels, or materially different goods returned. Employees must not accuse the customer or delay a statutory refund without authorization. The Returns Team Lead places the case in Review Required status and refers it to Customer Protection Operations. The review target is five business days. Confirmed abuse may result in account restrictions under the Customer Account Controls Standard, subject to Compliance review. Customer disputes about inspection outcomes are reviewed using warehouse photographs, scan history, carrier data, and previous case notes. A written decision is issued within five business days of receiving the dispute. 4.7 Final Disposition and Environmental Controls

Disposition must be completed within 15 calendar days of warehouse receipt unless a supplier or safety investigation is open. Approved options are:  Return to sellable stock.  Transfer to outlet or refurbished inventory.  Repair through an approved service partner.  Return to supplier under an authorized RMA.  Liquidation through an approved channel.  Recycling or controlled destruction. Employees must not place returned electronics, batteries, chemicals, textiles, or personal-care products in general waste. WEEE, batteries, packaging, and other regulated materials must be handled through approved waste contractors and recorded in the Environmental Compliance Register. Products suspected to be unsafe are quarantined immediately. The Quality & Compliance Manager determines whether a wider stock hold, supplier notification, customer notification, or regulatory report is required. 5. Roles and Responsibilities  Customer Service: Validate requests, communicate decisions, and maintain accurate customer-facing notes.  Returns Team Lead: Approve standard exceptions, monitor ageing cases, and coach inspection teams.  Warehouse Operations: Receive, scan, inspect, photograph, grade, and move returned stock.  Inventory Control: Confirm stock adjustments and prevent duplicate availability.  Finance Operations: Monitor refund execution, payment exceptions, and approval controls.  Customer Protection Operations: Investigate suspected abuse, fraud, and serial-number disputes.  Quality & Compliance: Manage safety, regulatory, environmental, and restricted-product issues.  Deliveries Operations Manager: Own the procedure, carrier performance, and monthly KPI review.  Approved repair and waste partners: Provide evidence of repair, recycling, destruction, or final disposition. 6. Controls and Reporting Deliveries Operations reviews the following indicators monthly:  Return

Deliveries Operations Manager: Own the procedure, carrier performance, and monthly KPI review.  Approved repair and waste partners: Provide evidence of repair, recycling, destruction, or final disposition. 6. Controls and Reporting Deliveries Operations reviews the following indicators monthly:  Return rate by category, country, supplier, and reason code.  Average days from receipt to resolution.  Refund ageing and unresolved-case volume.  Percentage of returns graded A–E.  Carrier return cost per parcel.  Fraud referrals and confirmed abuse.

 Percentage of stock with completed final disposition.  Safety or environmental incidents. Any KPI below target for two consecutive months requires a corrective-action owner and due date in the Operations Improvement Register. 7. Shipping & Delivery SLA Policy Owning area: Deliveries Last reviewed: August 2026 Policy ID: DEL-SLA-004 Effective date: 1 September 2026 Policy owner: Director of Delivery Operations 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines IronStore’s delivery service levels, operational requirements, escalation rules, and customer communication standards for orders shipped within the European Economic Area (EEA), the United Kingdom, and Switzerland. The policy applies from order release to confirmed delivery, including carrier handover, tracking, failed delivery, delays, damage, and loss. It establishes minimum service expectations for fulfilment centres, marketplace sellers, carriers, Customer Care, and Delivery Operations. Service levels are measured using timestamps from IronStore’s Order Management System (OMS), Warehouse Management System (WMS), and carrier tracking feeds. Unless a product page or checkout promise states a stricter commitment, this policy sets the applicable minimum standard. 2. Scope This policy covers:  Orders placed through the IronStore website, mobile application, and approved marketplace channels.  Standard, express, scheduled, click-and-collect, and bulky-item deliveries.  Shipments dispatched from IronStore fulfilment centres and approved merchant locations.  Delivery activity in EEA countries, the UK, and Switzerland.  Carrier performance, customer notifications, exception handling, and delivery claims. This policy does not cover:  Digital products, services, subscriptions, or gift-card-only orders.  Deliveries to restricted territories, military addresses, or unsupported forwarding services.  Delays caused solely by customer-requested changes after dispatch.  Product-specific installation or assembly services unless included in the order confirmation. 3. IronStore must provide a delivery promise that is achievable, location-specific, and based on current inventory, fulfilment capacity, carrier service, and cut-off times. The promise shown at checkout is the customer-facing SLA. Orders must be delivered within the promised window unless an approved exception applies. When a delivery risk is identified, IronStore must notify the customer promptly and provide a revised date or an available resolution. The standard delivery target is measured in calendar days from payment approval and order release. Public holidays, carrier non-operating days, and customer-requested delivery holds are excluded where stated at checkout. 4. Delivery Service Levels 4.1 Standard parcel delivery For in-stock products shipped from an IronStore fulfilment centre:  Domestic delivery: 2–4 working days after dispatch.  Cross-border EEA delivery: 3–7 working days after dispatch.  UK and Switzerland delivery: 4–8 working days after dispatch.  Dispatch target: within one working day of payment approval.  Orders placed after the published daily cut-off are treated as placed on the next working day. The checkout promise may be longer for remote areas, customs-controlled destinations, or seller-fulfilled products. 4.2 Express delivery Where offered:  Dispatch target: same working day for orders placed before the local cut-off.  Domestic delivery: next working day after dispatch.  Cross-border delivery: 1–3 working days after dispatch.  Express service must not be offered where carrier capacity, product dimensions, or destination restrictions make the promise unreliable. Express eligibility is determined by the Delivery Promise Engine and may not be manually overridden without approval

Express eligibility is determined by the Delivery Promise Engine and may not be manually overridden without approval from the Regional Delivery Manager. 4.3 Bulky and special-handling orders Bulky products, including furniture, large appliances, fitness equipment, and selected outdoor products, use a scheduled delivery service:  Customer contact within two working days of order release.  Delivery appointment offered within 5–12 working days, subject to postcode and capacity.  Two-person delivery, room-of-choice, installation, or disposal services must be confirmed in the order record.  Failed appointments caused by the customer may incur a rebooking charge where disclosed before purchase.

Split orders may arrive in separate consignments. The customer must receive a clear explanation of the expected sequence and any additional delivery charges before payment. 5. Operational Procedures 5.1 Order release and fulfilment The OMS releases orders to the WMS or approved merchant channel after payment approval and fraud screening. Fulfilment teams must:  Confirm stock allocation within four hours during operating hours.  Pick, pack, and manifest standard orders within the applicable dispatch target.  Use packaging appropriate to product dimensions, fragility, and regulatory requirements.  Scan the parcel at pack station and carrier handover.  Ensure the tracking number is linked to the correct order and customer notification. If stock becomes unavailable after checkout, the fulfilment centre must place the order in “inventory exception” status within two hours. Customer Care must be notified before the promised dispatch date. 5.2 Carrier handover and tracking Approved carriers must receive parcels against a manifest or electronic handover record. The first carrier scan should occur within 24 hours of manifest creation. Delivery Operations monitors:  No-scan shipments exceeding 36 hours.  Shipments with no movement for 48 hours.  Repeated failed delivery attempts.  Carrier status codes indicating damage, address problems, customs holds, or return to sender. The Carrier Performance Dashboard in Looker is the primary reporting source. Manual spreadsheets may be used only during system outages and must be reconciled within two working days. 5.3 Customer communication The following messages must be sent through the Notification Service:  Order confirmation after

Manual spreadsheets may be used only during system outages and must be reconciled within two working days. 5.3 Customer communication The following messages must be sent through the Notification Service:  Order confirmation after successful payment.  Dispatch confirmation with carrier name and tracking link.  Out-for-delivery notification where supported.  Delivery confirmation or collection-ready message.

 Delay, failed-delivery, or address-action notification when required. A delivery delay of more than one working day against the checkout promise requires proactive customer contact. The message must include:  Current shipment status.  Revised estimated delivery date.  Available customer options.  Customer Care contact route. Customer Care must not promise compensation, replacement, or refund outside the approved matrix without the required approval. 5.4 Address changes and delivery holds Before dispatch, address corrections may be made by Customer Care after customer verification. After dispatch:  Address changes must be requested through the carrier where supported.  Delivery holds require carrier confirmation and must be recorded in the OMS.  Any additional carrier charge requires customer approval before acceptance.  Fraud, account takeover, or high-value address changes must be referred to Trust & Safety. A customer-requested change resets the delivery commitment where the revised date is shown or explicitly accepted by the customer. 5.5 Failed delivery and returns For a first failed attempt, the carrier should provide a re-delivery, collection-point, or customer-rescheduling option where available. IronStore must review shipments after:  Two failed delivery attempts.  Five calendar days at a collection point.  A “return to sender” scan.  An address exception that remains unresolved for 24 hours. If a parcel is returned because of carrier error, IronStore must offer a replacement or refund without charging the customer. If the customer supplied an incomplete or incorrect address, resolution follows the Returns and Refunds Policy. 6. Exceptions, Claims, and Compensation

The following may suspend or extend the SLA:  Severe weather, flooding, natural disasters, or major transport disruption.  Customs inspection or missing import information.  Regulatory restrictions or border closures.  Carrier network outage or industrial action.  Customer-requested changes or unavailable delivery access.  Incorrect, incomplete, or refused delivery address. Delivery Operations must classify exceptions in the OMS using the approved reason code. General “carrier delay” is not sufficient where a more specific code is available. 6.2 Lost, damaged, or materially delayed parcels A parcel may be treated as potentially lost when:  There is no carrier movement for five calendar days after the expected delivery date; or  The carrier confirms loss; or  The parcel exceeds the carrier’s investigation threshold. Customer Care opens a claim in the Carrier Claims Portal and records the case number in the CRM. For damaged goods, photographs, packaging evidence, and product value must be requested where appropriate. Standard resolution targets are:  Initial customer response: within one working day.  Carrier claim submission: within two working days of confirmed exception.  Replacement or refund decision: within three working days after required evidence is received. Any goodwill credit above €25 requires Customer Care Team Lead approval. Credits above €100, repeated compensation, or claims involving regulated products require approval from the Customer Care Manager. 6.3 Performance targets Delivery Operations reports the following monthly measures by country, carrier, fulfilment site, and service type:  On-time delivery rate: at least 95%.  On-time dispatch rate:

claims involving regulated products require approval from the Customer Care Manager. 6.3 Performance targets Delivery Operations reports the following monthly measures by country, carrier, fulfilment site, and service type:  On-time delivery rate: at least 95%.  On-time dispatch rate: at least 97%.  First-attempt delivery success: at least 92%.  Parcel loss rate: below 0.30%.  Customer contacts caused by delivery failure: monitored monthly and reviewed for trend. A carrier below target for two consecutive months requires a corrective action plan. A third consecutive failure triggers a commercial review and may result in volume reduction or temporary suspension.

Warehouse Operations Manual Owning area: Deliveries Document ID: DEL-WH-001 Version: 3.2 Last reviewed: August 2026 Applies to: IronStore fulfilment centres and approved third-party logistics sites in Europe 1. Purpose and Overview This manual defines the minimum operating standards for receiving, storing, picking, packing, and dispatching IronStore customer orders. It is intended to support safe, accurate, and traceable warehouse operations across all product categories, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and other consumer goods. The procedures apply alongside local legal requirements, site instructions, carrier rules, and product-specific controls. Where a local requirement is stricter than this manual, the stricter requirement applies. Deviations must be recorded in the Atlas Warehouse Management System (WMS) and approved by the relevant Operations Manager. 2. Scope This manual covers:  Supplier and inter-site inbound deliveries.  Goods receiving, inspection, labelling, and putaway.  Inventory control, cycle counting, and location management.  Customer order picking, packing, and dispatch.  Returns, damaged stock, shortages, and delivery exceptions.  Warehouse safety, security, and operational reporting. It does not replace:  Dangerous goods procedures under HSE-PRO-014.  Transport planning and carrier procurement rules under DEL-TMS-002.  Product compliance, recall, or restricted-goods procedures.  Site-specific emergency plans and risk assessments. 3. Policy Statement IronStore warehouses must process stock and orders accurately, safely, and within the service levels agreed with the Deliveries function. Every stock movement must be recorded electronically, and every dispatch must be traceable to an order, parcel, carrier, and operator or system event.

The booking must include:  Supplier or origin site.  Purchase order or transfer order number.  Pallet, carton, and expected unit quantities.  Product type and any handling restrictions.  Carrier, vehicle registration, and estimated arrival time. The Inbound Team checks the appointment against the purchase order before unloading. Unscheduled vehicles may be held in the designated waiting area and must not unload without approval from the Inbound Supervisor. The gatehouse or receiving desk records arrival and departure times. Drivers must follow site traffic controls, wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), and remain in the designated area unless escorted. 4.2 Unloading and Receiving Before unloading, the receiving operator checks:  Vehicle condition and signs of water, pest, or security damage.  Seal number, where applicable.  Pallet stability and visible carton damage.  Quantity of handling units against the delivery note. Goods are unloaded only at the assigned bay. A second operator verifies the count for deliveries exceeding 20 pallets

A second operator verifies the count for deliveries exceeding 20 pallets or 500 units. The operator scans the purchase order or transfer order into Atlas WMS and records received quantities by SKU, batch, serial number, and expiry date where required. System receipt is completed on the same working day. Shortages, overages, substitutions, and unlisted SKUs are placed in the Inbound Hold location. The Inbound Supervisor contacts Procurement or the sending site within four working hours. Stock may not be released for sale

until the discrepancy is resolved or formally approved. 4.3 Inspection and Product Controls A sample inspection is performed on each inbound delivery. The standard sample is:  Five cartons for deliveries of up to 100 cartons.  Ten cartons for deliveries over 100 cartons.  The full delivery where damage or repeated quality issues are identified. Operators check packaging, labels, product identity, accessories, and visible defects. Electronics with serial numbers must be scanned individually. Beauty products, food-contact items, and other dated goods must meet the minimum remaining shelf-life specified in the purchase order. Damaged or suspect stock is labelled QUARANTINE – DO NOT SHIP, moved to the secure quarantine area, and photographed in Atlas WMS. The Quality Lead decides whether stock is released, reworked, returned, or scrapped. Staff must not repair, repackage, or relabel goods without documented approval. 4.4 Putaway and Storage Atlas WMS generates the putaway task based on product dimensions, turnover, handling restrictions, and location capacity. Operators must scan both the product and destination location before placing stock. Storage rules include:  Heavy items below shoulder height.  Fragile items in protected shelving or designated cages.  High-value electronics in access-controlled locations.  Aerosols, liquids, batteries, and other controlled products in approved areas.  Clothing and textiles kept dry and protected from contamination.  Expiry-controlled stock managed using FEFO: first expiry, first out. A location must not exceed its weight, volume, or pallet-height limit. Empty locations are kept clear, labelled, and available in Atlas WMS. Any unlabelled or

Empty locations are kept clear, labelled, and available in Atlas WMS. Any unlabelled or inaccessible location is reported to the Inventory Controller. 4.5 Inventory Accuracy All stock adjustments require a reason code and electronic approval. The following approval levels apply:  Up to €50 cost value: Inventory Controller.  €50.01–€500: Warehouse Operations Manager.  Above €500, repeated variance, or suspected theft: Head of Deliveries and Loss Prevention. Cycle counts are completed daily according to the Atlas WMS count queue. A location is recounted when the first count differs from the system by more than:

 One unit for serialized products.  Two units or 2%, whichever is greater, for standard products.  One case for case-managed inventory. The counter must not edit the expected quantity before completing the recount. Variances are investigated using receiving records, pick scans, replenishment tasks, and dispatch confirmations. 4.6 Picking Customer orders are released to the warehouse through Atlas WMS according to the cut-off schedule published by Planning. The default same-day release cut-off is 14:00 local time, although site-specific cut-offs may differ. Picking operators must: 1. Scan the task, location, and product. 2. Confirm quantity and, where required, serial number or batch. 3. Place items in the assigned tote or container. 4. Report empty, damaged, or incorrect stock immediately. 5. Close the task only after the physical movement is complete. Operators must not pick from a location showing a quarantine, blocked, or investigation status. Substitutions are prohibited unless approved by Customer Care and enabled in the order system. For multi-item orders, totes must remain separated by order or wave. Totes left unattended for more than 30 minutes must be returned to the designated staging area. 4.7 Packing and Quality Check Packing stations must use the packaging recommendation displayed in Atlas WMS. The packer confirms:  Correct order and recipient details.  Product quantity and condition.  Required accessories, documents, and promotional inserts.  Carrier service and destination country.  Packaging suitability and closure. A second check is required for high-value orders, orders containing more than five SKUs, and any order

 Product quantity and condition.  Required accessories, documents, and promotional inserts.  Carrier service and destination country.  Packaging suitability and closure. A second check is required for high-value orders, orders containing more than five SKUs, and any order flagged by the fraud or Customer Care systems. The checker records the verification in Atlas WMS. Packages must be sealed securely, with no loose labels or exposed product. Customer information must not be visible through transparent packaging. Batteries, liquids, aerosols, and fragile goods require the approved inner protection and external markings. The packer prints the carrier label only after the parcel weight is recorded. A weight variance above 10% from the system expectation triggers a recheck before dispatch.

4.8 Dispatch and Handover Completed parcels are scanned into the correct carrier cage or dispatch lane. Carrier manifests are generated in Mercury TMS and reconciled against the physical parcel count before loading. The Dispatch Supervisor verifies:  Parcel count by carrier and service.  Manifest totals and exception parcels.  Cage or vehicle seal number.  Collection time and driver identity. No parcel may be handed to a carrier without a successful dispatch scan. Missed collections, rejected parcels, or manifest differences are logged in the Delivery Incident Register within one hour. Standard dispatch targets are:  98.5% of parcels scanned before the carrier collection cut-off.  99.7% order-pick accuracy.  99.5% parcel-to-manifest reconciliation.  Same-day escalation for any lost or untraceable parcel. 4.9 Returns and Delivery Exceptions Customer returns are received against a return authorisation or carrier return reference. The Returns Team classifies each item as:  Resalable.  Open-box or rework required.  Damaged.  Incomplete.  Suspected counterfeit or compliance concern. The classification, photographs, and disposition are recorded in Atlas WMS within two working days. Refund decisions remain with Customer Care and Finance. Delivery exceptions, including wrong item, missing parcel, damage in transit, or address failure, are recorded against the original order. The Deliveries Support Desk owns carrier enquiries and must issue the first status update within one working day. Suspected theft, deliberate damage, or repeated carrier loss is escalated to Loss Prevention and the Head of Deliveries. 5. Safety, Security, and Housekeeping
