Budget Approval Workflow Owning area: Finance Policy ID: FIN-PR-014 Last reviewed: August 2026 Effective date: 1 September 2026 Applies to: IronStore entities and employees across Europe Purpose and Overview This workflow defines how IronStore requests, reviews, approves, records, and monitors expenditure. It applies to operating costs, capital expenditure, marketing spend, technology investments, logistics projects, supplier commitments, and other purchases made on behalf of the company. The workflow is intended to ensure that spending is:  Within an approved budget or properly justified as unplanned.  Supported by a clear business need and documented supplier terms.  Approved by the correct budget owner and financial authority.  Compliant with procurement, tax, legal, information security, and delegated-authority requirements.  Recorded accurately in IronStore’s financial systems before a commitment is made. No employee may commit IronStore funds, sign a supplier order, or instruct a supplier to begin work before the required approvals are complete. Scope This policy covers:  Purchase orders, statements of work, subscriptions, advertising commitments, and supplier contracts.  One-time and recurring expenditure, including renewals and automatic extensions.  Capital expenditure, such as warehouse equipment, software development, fixtures, and infrastructure.  Employee expenses where the cost was not already covered by an approved purchase order.  Spend made by IronStore legal entities in the EU, UK, Switzerland, and other European operating markets. This policy does not replace:  The Procurement and Supplier Due Diligence Standard (PROC-STD-003).  The Delegation of Authority Matrix (FIN-MAT-002).  Local tax, employment, data protection, or statutory

entities in the EU, UK, Switzerland, and other European operating markets. This policy does not replace:  The Procurement and Supplier Due Diligence Standard (PROC-STD-003).  The Delegation of Authority Matrix (FIN-MAT-002).  Local tax, employment, data protection, or statutory accounting requirements. Where local law or a customer-contract obligation is stricter, the stricter requirement applies.

Policy Statement All expenditure must have: 1. A named business owner. 2. An approved cost centre and, where applicable, project code. 3. A documented commercial rationale. 4. A valid approval in Coupa, IronStore’s purchasing and approval platform. 5. A purchase order or approved contract before goods or services are ordered. 6. A matching invoice, receipt, or delivery confirmation before payment. Approvals may not be split across invoices, suppliers, projects, or accounting periods to avoid an approval threshold. A commitment includes the full expected value, including extensions, implementation fees, minimum usage charges, taxes that cannot be recovered, and the initial contract term. Approvers must not approve their own expenses, their own compensation, or expenditure from which they receive a personal benefit. Finance may reject, hold, or escalate transactions that do not meet this policy. Budget Approval Procedure 1. Define the request The requester creates a Spend Request in Coupa before contacting a supplier or confirming an order. The request must include:  Description of the product, service, or project.  Business purpose and expected outcome.  Total committed value in EUR, excluding recoverable VAT.  Contract term, renewal date, and cancellation terms.  Supplier name or proposed sourcing approach.  Cost centre, general ledger category, and project code.  Expected delivery date and payment schedule.  Confirmation that the cost is in the approved annual budget. For foreign-currency commitments, the requester records the EUR equivalent using the monthly Finance planning rate in NetSuite. Finance may update the value using the contracted

date and payment schedule.  Confirmation that the cost is in the approved annual budget. For foreign-currency commitments, the requester records the EUR equivalent using the monthly Finance planning rate in NetSuite. Finance may update the value using the contracted exchange rate before final approval. 2. Check budget availability The budget owner checks the request against the current plan in Anaplan and the actuals in Oracle NetSuite. The request must identify one of the following:

 Budgeted spend: Covered by the current approved plan.  Budget transfer: Covered by another cost centre or project and requiring a documented reallocation.  Unplanned spend: Not included in the approved plan and requiring additional approval.  Renewal spend: A recurring commitment that must be reassessed before renewal, even if previously approved. Budget availability does not itself authorise the purchase. Approval must still follow the thresholds below. 3. Obtain commercial and specialist review Before financial approval, the requester obtains the relevant reviews:  Procurement: Required for new suppliers, competitive sourcing, or spend above €25,000.  Legal: Required for contracts, data processing, intellectual property, exclusivity, unusual liability, or non-standard terms.  Information Security: Required for software, hosted services, integrations, customer data, or access to IronStore systems.  Tax: Required for cross-border arrangements, unusual VAT treatment, customs, royalties, or withholding-tax exposure.  People Team: Required for recruitment agencies, contractors, employee benefits, or workforce-related services. Coupa routes required reviews based on category, supplier, entity, and value. Reviewers record conditions or exceptions directly in the request. 4. Apply approval thresholds Approval thresholds are based on the total expected commitment per supplier and business need. The following minimum chain applies:  Up to €5,000: Cost centre owner.  €5,001–€25,000: Cost centre owner and department director.  €25,001–€100,000: Department director and regional Finance Business Partner.  €100,001–€500,000: Executive sponsor, Finance Director, and Procurement Director.  Above €500,000: Executive sponsor, CFO, and CEO or designated Executive Committee member. Additional requirements:  Capital expenditure above €50,000: Finance

director.  €25,001–€100,000: Department director and regional Finance Business Partner.  €100,001–€500,000: Executive sponsor, Finance Director, and Procurement Director.  Above €500,000: Executive sponsor, CFO, and CEO or designated Executive Committee member. Additional requirements:  Capital expenditure above €50,000: Finance Business Partner and CFO delegate must confirm the asset classification, useful life, and capital budget.  Marketing commitments above €100,000: Chief Marketing Officer or delegate must approve the commercial plan and performance measures.  Technology commitments above €100,000: Chief Technology Officer or delegate must approve architecture, security, and implementation capacity.

 New or renewed contracts with a term exceeding 36 months: Legal and CFO delegate approval are required regardless of value.  Multi-year commitments: Approval is based on the full contract value, not the annual instalment. An approver may delegate authority only through the approved Coupa delegation function. Email approval is not sufficient unless Coupa is unavailable and Finance has authorised the exception. 5. Complete sourcing and contracting Procurement determines the sourcing method:  Up to €25,000: documented price or market check where practical.  €25,001–€100,000: normally at least two competitive quotations.  Above €100,000: normally a formal tender with at least three qualified suppliers. A sole-source or emergency exception requires a written justification in Coupa and Procurement approval. The justification must explain the supplier dependency, urgency, market constraints, or technical compatibility. Only authorised signatories may execute supplier contracts. A purchase order is not a substitute for a contract where legal, data protection, or commercial terms require a signed agreement. 6. Issue the purchase order After all approvals are complete, Procurement or the authorised requester converts the approved request into a purchase order. The supplier must receive the purchase order before delivery or service commencement. The purchase order must state:  Legal entity and billing address.  Supplier details and tax registration information.  Approved value and currency.  Payment terms and delivery requirements.  Cost centre, project code, and requester.  Applicable contract or statement of work reference. Invoices without a valid purchase order are placed on hold unless

tax registration information.  Approved value and currency.  Payment terms and delivery requirements.  Cost centre, project code, and requester.  Applicable contract or statement of work reference. Invoices without a valid purchase order are placed on hold unless Finance approves a documented exception. 7. Monitor delivery and invoice matching The requester confirms receipt of goods or completion of services in Coupa. Accounts Payable performs a three-way match between: 1. Approved purchase order. 2. Receipt or service confirmation. 3. Supplier invoice.

Discrepancies are resolved by the requester, Procurement, or supplier. Accounts Payable does not amend an approved order to conceal an overspend. The requester must review recurring services at least 30 days before renewal. The review must confirm continued business need, supplier performance, pricing, user volumes, and cancellation deadlines. Unplanned, Urgent, and Exceptional Spend Unplanned spend follows the normal approval chain and must identify the funding source. Finance may require a forecast update or budget transfer before approval. Urgent spend is limited to situations involving:  Customer, employee, or physical safety.  Material interruption to fulfilment, payment, logistics, or core systems.  Legal or regulatory deadlines.  Significant risk of financial loss if action is delayed. The requester must obtain verbal approval from the relevant executive or Finance leader and document it in Coupa within two business days. Procurement and Legal must be informed as soon as practicable. Convenience, supplier pressure, missed planning deadlines, or a favourable discount do not qualify as urgent circumstances. Petty cash, personal cards, or direct supplier payments must not be used to bypass this workflow. Repeated exceptions may result in suspension of purchasing access or disciplinary action. Roles and Responsibilities  Requester: Defines the need, provides accurate information, monitors delivery, and confirms receipt.  Budget owner: Confirms business priority, budget availability, and value for money.  Department director: Reviews material departmental commitments and operational impact.  Finance Business Partner: Validates funding, accounting treatment, forecast impact, and thresholds.  Procurement: Manages sourcing, supplier onboarding, competitive bids, and

Confirms business priority, budget availability, and value for money.  Department director: Reviews material departmental commitments and operational impact.  Finance Business Partner: Validates funding, accounting treatment, forecast impact, and thresholds.  Procurement: Manages sourcing, supplier onboarding, competitive bids, and purchase orders.  Legal: Reviews contractual, regulatory, liability, intellectual property, and data protection matters.  Information Security: Assesses technology, access, hosting, and security risks.  Accounts Payable: Performs invoice controls, tax checks, and payment processing.  CFO: Owns this policy, approves designated high-value commitments, and resolves escalations.  Internal Audit: Tests compliance and reports material control failures to the Audit Committee. Records, Controls, and Reporting Coupa is the system of record for purchase approvals, sourcing evidence, purchase orders, and exceptions. NetSuite is the system of record for accounting entries, invoices, accruals, and payments. Anaplan is the system of record for budgets, forecasts, and approved planning assumptions.

Records must be retained for at least seven years, or longer where local law, a contract, or a litigation hold requires it. Finance publishes a monthly report covering:  Approved versus actual spend by cost centre.  Open purchase orders and unused commitments.  Unplanned and exception spend.  Contract renewals due within 90 days.  Invoices received without purchase orders.  Approval breaches and overdue remediation. IronStore Expense Reimbursement Policy Policy ID: FIN-EXP-004 Owning area: Finance Effective date: 1 September 2026 Last reviewed: August 2026 Policy owner: Director of Financial Control 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines how IronStore employees and approved contractors may incur, document, approve, and claim business expenses. It applies to spending made on behalf of IronStore in connection with work activities, including travel, meetings, customer or supplier events, and approved home-working requirements. IronStore reimburses reasonable, necessary, and properly documented expenses. Employees must use company payment methods where available and select cost-effective options. Personal spending must not be used to bypass purchasing controls, approval limits, or supplier onboarding requirements. Expenses are processed through SpendHub, IronStore’s expense management system. Approved claims are paid through the employee’s normal payroll or bank payment process, subject to local payroll and tax rules. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  All IronStore employees in European entities.  Temporary workers and contractors where their contract permits reimbursement.  Directors and senior leaders, unless a stricter local or board policy applies.  Expenses paid personally or with an IronStore corporate card.  Business travel, accommodation, meals, mileage, business hospitality, and approved incidental costs. This policy does not cover:  Supplier invoices or purchase orders, which must follow the Procurement and Purchase Order Policy.  Relocation, immigration, or expatriate benefits.  Salary, bonus, or other employment benefits.  Personal commuting between home and the employee’s normal workplace.  Expenses prohibited by local law or an employee’s employment contract. Where local legislation provides a stricter requirement, the local requirement takes precedence. Finance may issue country-specific guidance for tax, VAT, mileage, or payroll treatment. 3. Policy Statement

3.1 General requirements Employees must ensure that each expense is:  Necessary for a legitimate IronStore business purpose.  Reasonable in amount and proportionate to the activity.  In line with this policy and any approved budget.  Supported by a valid receipt or other acceptable evidence.  Submitted within the required timeframe.  Charged to the correct legal entity, department, project, and cost centre. Employees must not approve their own expenses, split a transaction to avoid an approval threshold, or claim an expense more than once. Deliberate misuse may result in repayment, disciplinary action, or referral to Legal or Internal Audit. The most economical practical option should be selected. A more expensive option may be used where it saves significant working time, supports accessibility needs, or is justified by operational requirements. 3.2 Corporate cards Corporate cards are issued through SpendHub Cards and are intended for approved business spending only. Cardholders must:  Keep the card secure and never share card details.  Use the card for travel bookings and recurring business expenses where practical.  Upload receipts and business descriptions within five calendar days.  Reconcile the monthly card statement by the fifth working day of the following month.  Report lost cards or suspected fraud immediately to the bank and Finance Operations. Personal purchases, cash withdrawals, fines, and entertainment unrelated to business are not permitted on a corporate card. Accidental personal charges must be reported in SpendHub and repaid within ten working days. 3.3 Pre-approval requirements Written pre-approval

bank and Finance Operations. Personal purchases, cash withdrawals, fines, and entertainment unrelated to business are not permitted on a corporate card. Accidental personal charges must be reported in SpendHub and repaid within ten working days. 3.3 Pre-approval requirements Written pre-approval is required before committing to:  Any international business trip.  Accommodation expected to exceed €200 per night, excluding taxes.  Events, hospitality, or team activities exceeding €75 per attendee.  Any single expense or booking above €1,000.  Business-class rail or air travel.  Travel involving a customer, supplier, or public official.

 Expenses outside an approved project or departmental budget. Pre-approval is recorded in SpendHub or, for travel, in TravelPerk. The approval chain is normally: 1. Line manager. 2. Budget owner, where different. 3. Finance Business Partner for exceptions or higher-risk items. 4. Executive sponsor for commitments above €5,000. Emergency spending may proceed without advance approval where delay would create a material business risk. The employee must document the reason and obtain retrospective approval within five working days. 3.4 Travel and transport Travel must be booked through TravelPerk, using the employee’s assigned country profile and approved payment method. Permitted standards are:  Economy class for flights and rail journeys under six hours.  Premium economy for journeys exceeding six hours, where available and reasonably priced.  Business class only with CFO approval or documented medical accommodation.  Standard or equivalent rail fare unless a flexible ticket is needed for business reasons.  Mid-range hotels with a normal business rate for the destination.  Public transport, licensed taxis, and approved ride-hailing services.  Rental cars in the compact or intermediate category unless equipment or passenger needs require more. Travel should generally be booked at least 14 days in advance. Changes or cancellations must be made promptly to reduce fees. Seat upgrades, lounge access, minibar charges, in-room entertainment, and personal insurance are not reimbursable unless specifically approved. Employees may use a private vehicle for business travel where practical. Mileage is reimbursed at the applicable national rate published by Finance, currently €0.30 per business

access, minibar charges, in-room entertainment, and personal insurance are not reimbursable unless specifically approved. Employees may use a private vehicle for business travel where practical. Mileage is reimbursed at the applicable national rate published by Finance, currently €0.30 per business kilometre in countries using the standard IronStore rate. The claim must show date, origin, destination, purpose, and kilometres. Normal commuting is excluded. 3.5 Meals and subsistence Reasonable meals during approved business travel may be reimbursed within the following maximums:  Breakfast: €15.  Lunch: €25.  Dinner: €45.  Daily incidental allowance: €10, where permitted by local tax rules. The allowance is not payable where a meal is provided by IronStore, a hotel, an event organiser, or a customer. Alcohol is not reimbursable as a personal travel expense. A modest amount of alcohol may be included in an

approved business meal where customary and appropriate. Meal claims must identify all attendees when another person’s meal is included. The claimant must state the business purpose and identify any customer, supplier, or public-sector attendee. 3.6 Business hospitality and team activities Hospitality must have a clear business purpose and must not create an actual or perceived conflict of interest. It must be modest, infrequent, and appropriate to the relationship. Claims must include:  Date and venue.  Business purpose.  Names, organisations, and roles of attendees.  Total amount and currency.  Approval evidence where pre-approval was required. Hospitality involving public officials, regulators, or government-owned entities requires review by Legal and Compliance before the commitment is made. Cash gifts, gift cards, personal gifts, and facilitation payments are prohibited. Team meals and events may be reimbursed when approved by the department head and charged to the relevant team budget. The normal limit is €75 per attendee, including taxes and service charges. Events must not exclude employees on the basis of protected characteristics or religious observance. 3.7 Home-working and incidental expenses Employees may claim approved business equipment or home-working supplies only where the item is not available through IronStore’s standard equipment catalogue. Requests must be submitted through ServiceNow before purchase. Examples of potentially reimbursable items include:  Ergonomic accessories approved by Workplace Services.  Required stationery or shipping materials.  Business calls or connectivity costs where no company alternative exists.  Work-related visas, vaccinations, or travel documentation. Furniture, utilities, broadband, and personal office

reimbursable items include:  Ergonomic accessories approved by Workplace Services.  Required stationery or shipping materials.  Business calls or connectivity costs where no company alternative exists.  Work-related visas, vaccinations, or travel documentation. Furniture, utilities, broadband, and personal office improvements are not reimbursable unless expressly covered by the employee’s local employment terms or a country-specific agreement. 3.8 Receipts, VAT, and foreign currency Original itemised receipts are required for expenses of €25 or more, or for any expense where local tax rules require evidence. Bank or card statements alone are not sufficient.

A compliant receipt should show:  Supplier name and date.  Items or services purchased.  Amount, currency, and applicable VAT.  VAT number where relevant. If a receipt is unavailable, the employee must complete the Missing Receipt Declaration in SpendHub, explain the circumstances, and obtain manager approval. Repeated missing receipts may result in claim rejection or suspension of card privileges. Foreign-currency expenses are converted using the card settlement rate. Personal payments are converted using the European Central Bank rate on the transaction date, as calculated by SpendHub. Employees must not claim foreign-exchange mark-ups, exchange fees, or cash withdrawal fees unless directly incurred for business purposes and documented. 3.9 Submission, review, and payment Claims must be submitted in SpendHub within 30 calendar days of the expense date. Month-end claims should be submitted by the third working day of the following month. Claims submitted more than 90 days late require Finance Director approval. The claimant must select the correct:  Legal entity.  Cost centre.  Project or campaign code.  Expense category.  VAT treatment. Line managers review business purpose, reasonableness, and budget availability. Finance Operations checks documentation, tax treatment, duplicate claims, and policy compliance. Approved claims are normally paid within the next available payroll or weekly accounts-payable run, depending on the employee’s country. Rejected claims are returned through SpendHub with a reason. The employee may correct and resubmit within 15 calendar days. Disputes should first be raised with the line manager and then with the Finance Operations Manager. 4.

This procedure does not replace local employment law, collective agreements, tax rules, or country-specific payroll instructions. Where requirements conflict, the stricter statutory requirement applies and Payroll Legal Counsel must be consulted. 3. Policy Statement IronStore pays employees accurately, on time, and in the

not replace local employment law, collective agreements, tax rules, or country-specific payroll instructions. Policy Statement IronStore pays employees accurately, on time, and in the currency specified in their employment contract. Payroll changes must be supported by an approved source document and entered into the designated system before the monthly cut-off.

Payroll information is confidential personal data. Access is limited to personnel with a documented business need and is managed according to the Information Security and Data Protection policies. Payroll files must not be sent through personal email, unsecured messaging applications, or unapproved file-sharing services. No individual may create, amend, approve, and release the same payroll payment without independent review. Bank payment release always requires two authorised approvers. 4. Monthly Payroll Procedure 4.1 Payroll Calendar and Cut-Offs The Payroll Operations Manager publishes the annual payroll calendar in January and updates it for country-specific holidays. Standard monthly deadlines are:  Working day 1: Previous month closes; payroll input period opens.  Working day 5: Managers submit approved variable-pay and absence adjustments.  Working day 7: People Operations closes employee master-data changes.  Working day 9: Payroll prepares the preliminary payroll run.  Working day 11: Finance completes variance review and control checks.  Working day 13: Country payroll owner and Finance Controller approve payroll.  Working day 15: Payment file and statutory payment instructions are released.  25th calendar day: Employees receive net pay, subject to bank processing times. Late submissions require approval from the Head of Payroll Operations. Changes received after payroll approval are normally processed in the following month unless legally or financially material. 4.2 Required Payroll Inputs Payroll inputs must be submitted through Workday, ServiceNow HR cases, or the approved country payroll portal. Email instructions alone are not sufficient. Required inputs may include:  New starters, transfers, promotions, salary

legally or financially material. 4.2 Required Payroll Inputs Payroll inputs must be submitted through Workday, ServiceNow HR cases, or the approved country payroll portal. Email instructions alone are not sufficient. Required inputs may include:  New starters, transfers, promotions, salary changes, and contract amendments.  Leavers, termination dates, notice payments, and unused holiday balances.  Approved overtime, shift premiums, commissions, sales incentives, and bonuses.  Sickness, parental leave, unpaid leave, and other absence adjustments.  Employee benefits, salary sacrifice, company car values, and taxable allowances.  Expense reimbursements approved under the Travel and Expenses Policy.  Court orders, statutory deductions, pension changes, and employee-requested deductions.

Every input must identify the employee, effective date, amount or rate, country, cost centre, and approving manager. Backdated changes must include the reason for the delay. 4.3 Employee Master Data People Operations owns employee master data. Payroll may update bank details, tax information, or payment preferences only after receiving an authenticated request and completing verification. Bank-account changes require:  Employee submission through Workday or the secure HR portal.  Confirmation against the employee’s existing contact record.  Independent review by a Payroll Specialist.  A minimum 24-hour cooling-off period before payment release, where operationally possible. Requests received by telephone or from an unfamiliar email address must not be actioned without identity verification. Any suspected payroll diversion or social-engineering attempt must be escalated immediately to Information Security and the Financial Control Manager. 4.4 Payroll Calculation and Review Payroll is calculated in CloudPay, using approved country configurations and data received from Workday. Local payroll bureaus may prepare calculations for jurisdictions where IronStore has outsourced processing. The Payroll Specialist performs the first-level review, including:  Employee count compared with the prior month.  Gross pay, net pay, employer cost, and statutory liability movements.  New starters and leavers.  Salary changes and one-time payments.  Negative net pay or unusually high deductions.  Duplicate bank accounts, duplicate employees, or missing payment details.  Country-specific tax, social-security, pension, and benefit calculations. The preliminary payroll report is reviewed against the prior month and the approved headcount report. Variances above the following thresholds require documented investigation:

Duplicate bank accounts, duplicate employees, or missing payment details.  Country-specific tax, social-security, pension, and benefit calculations. The preliminary payroll report is reviewed against the prior month and the approved headcount report. Variances above the following thresholds require documented investigation:  5% movement in total gross payroll for a country.  10% movement in an individual employee’s gross pay, excluding approved annual increases.  €1,000 change in an individual employee’s net pay.  Any unexplained change in statutory liabilities or employer taxes. The Payroll Specialist records explanations in the Payroll Control Checklist. Supporting documents must be attached to the payroll case or stored in the restricted Finance SharePoint library.

4.5 Approval Chain Payroll approval follows this sequence: 1. Payroll Specialist completes the preliminary calculation and checklist. 2. Country Payroll Owner confirms local compliance and input completeness. 3. Finance Controller reviews variances, reconciliations, and accounting coding. 4. Head of Payroll Operations approves the final payroll register. 5. Treasury prepares and releases payments under the dual-authorisation bank mandate. A payroll with unresolved material exceptions must not be approved. Exceptions below €500 may be approved by the Finance Controller when the issue is documented and correction timing is agreed. Exceptions of €500 or more, potential underpayments, or statutory compliance risks require approval from the Head of Payroll Operations. 4.6 Payment Processing After final approval, Payroll exports the net-pay file from CloudPay and uploads it to Kyriba for payment preparation. Statutory tax, social-security, pension, and third-party payment files are prepared separately where required. Treasury must verify:  File total agrees to the approved payroll register.  Number of employees agrees to the payment report.  Bank account and currency information is complete.  Payment date is consistent with the payroll calendar.  Payment file has not been amended after approval. Two authorised Treasury or Finance approvers must release the bank payment. Approvers must review the payment summary and may not approve a payment they prepared. Returned or rejected payments are recorded in ServiceNow and investigated within two business days. Reissued payments require confirmation of the corrected bank details and approval from Payroll Operations. 4.7 Accounting and Reconciliation Following payment, Payroll posts the payroll

they prepared. Returned or rejected payments are recorded in ServiceNow and investigated within two business days. Reissued payments require confirmation of the corrected bank details and approval from Payroll Operations. 4.7 Accounting and Reconciliation Following payment, Payroll posts the payroll journal to NetSuite using the approved entity, department, cost-centre, and account mapping. The monthly reconciliation must cover:  Payroll register to bank payment total.  Payroll journal to the approved payroll register.  Gross wages to payroll expense accounts.  Employee deductions to liability accounts.  Employer taxes and social charges to statutory liability accounts.

 Pension, benefit, and third-party remittances.  Accruals for bonuses, commissions, holiday pay, and unpaid payroll items. The Finance Accountant completes the reconciliation by the fifth business day of the following month. Unreconciled differences must be assigned to an owner with a target resolution date. Aged items over 30 days are reported to the Financial Control Manager. 4.8 Payslips and Employee Queries Payslips are issued through the secure Workday Employee Portal after payment release. Payroll must not send payslips as unencrypted email attachments. Employees should raise payroll queries through ServiceNow within 30 days of receiving the payslip. Payroll acknowledges queries within one business day and aims to resolve standard issues within five business days. Urgent cases include:  Missed salary payments.  Suspected unauthorised deductions.  Incorrect termination payments.  Potential tax or social-security errors.  Disclosure of another employee’s payroll information. Urgent cases are escalated to the Payroll Operations Manager and People Operations on the same business day. 5. Data Protection and Record Retention Payroll records must be stored in restricted folders with role-based access and audit logging. Access is reviewed quarterly by the Payroll Operations Manager and Finance Systems Administrator. Payroll records must be retained according to the FIN-REC-002 Records Retention Schedule and applicable local law. As a minimum:  Payroll registers, journals, approvals, and reconciliations: seven years.  Tax, social-security, pension, and statutory filings: statutory period, or seven years where no longer period applies.  Employee bank details and identity documents: only for the approved employment and

minimum:  Payroll registers, journals, approvals, and reconciliations: seven years.  Tax, social-security, pension, and statutory filings: statutory period, or seven years where no longer period applies.  Employee bank details and identity documents: only for the approved employment and legal retention period.  Temporary working files: deleted within 90 days after completion of the relevant reconciliation. Data incidents must be reported through the Security Incident Portal immediately and no later than four hours after discovery. 6. Roles and Responsibilities  Payroll Operations Manager: Owns the procedure, calendar, controls, escalations, and provider performance.  Payroll Specialist: Collects inputs, runs payroll, performs first-level checks, and maintains evidence.

 Country Payroll Owner: Confirms local compliance and validates country-specific calculations.  People Operations: Maintains employee records, contracts, absences, and approved changes.  Managers: Submit accurate and timely variable-pay, absence, and approval information.  Finance Controller: Reviews variances, reconciliations, accounting treatment, and material exceptions.  Treasury: Funds, validates, and releases payroll and statutory payments.  Finance Systems Administrator: Manages system access, integrations, and audit logs.  Employees: Review payslips and report suspected errors promptly. 7. Employee Handbook Owning area: HR_policies Last reviewed: August 2026 Document owner: Director of People Operations Policy ID: HR-001 Applies to: IronStore employees, fixed-term staff, interns, and agency workers where stated 1. Purpose and Overview This handbook sets out the main workplace standards, procedures, and employee benefits applicable across IronStore. IronStore is a European e-commerce company serving customers across multiple markets and product categories, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and related consumer goods. The handbook provides a common baseline for conduct and employment practices. Local law, employment contracts, collective agreements, and formally adopted country addenda take precedence where they provide different or stronger rights. Employees must read this handbook during onboarding and confirm completion in PeopleHub. Questions should be raised with the employee’s manager or the People Operations Helpdesk. 2. Scope This handbook applies to:  Employees working from IronStore offices, warehouses, or approved remote locations.  Employees supporting commercial, technology, fulfilment, customer service, finance, and corporate functions.  Temporary staff and contractors when using IronStore systems or representing IronStore.  All work-related activities, including business travel, company events, and online communications. Country-specific requirements are maintained in PeopleHub > Policies > Country Addenda. Employees must follow the rules applicable to their employing entity and work location. 3. Employment Standards and Workplace Conduct 3.1 Equal treatment and inclusion IronStore is committed to a respectful workplace. Employment decisions are based on skills, performance, qualifications, and business requirements. Discrimination, harassment, bullying, victimisation, or retaliation is not permitted on the basis

Employment Standards and Workplace Conduct 3.1 Equal treatment and inclusion IronStore is committed to a respectful workplace. Employment decisions are based on skills, performance, qualifications, and business requirements. Discrimination, harassment, bullying, victimisation, or retaliation is not permitted on the basis of protected characteristics under applicable law, including:

 Race, ethnic origin, nationality, or language.  Sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, or pregnancy.  Disability, age, religion, belief, or family status.  Health status, trade union activity, or any other legally protected ground. Employees should report concerns promptly to their manager, People Partner, or the confidential Speak Up Line. Reports are handled discreetly and investigated by authorised personnel. 3.2 Professional behaviour Employees are expected to:  Communicate respectfully with colleagues, customers, suppliers, and delivery partners.  Follow reasonable management instructions and approved operating procedures.  Protect confidential information and use company resources appropriately.  Declare conflicts of interest before participating in related decisions.  Keep records accurate, complete, and suitable for audit. Threatening behaviour, intimidation, violence, deliberate dishonesty, and working while impaired by alcohol or drugs may result in disciplinary action. 3.3 Dress and personal presentation Dress should be appropriate to the role, workplace, safety requirements, and customer or supplier interaction. Warehouse and operational employees must wear required protective equipment. Managers may provide reasonable role-specific guidance without applying discriminatory standards. 4. Working Arrangements and Attendance 4.1 Working hours Working hours are stated in the employment contract or local schedule. Employees must comply with applicable working-time, rest-break, and maximum-hours rules. For standard office roles:  Core collaboration hours are normally 09:30–15:30 local time.  Teams may set different coverage hours for customer support, fulfilment, and incident response.  Overtime or additional hours require advance manager approval, except in emergencies.  Employees must record time where required by local law

normally 09:30–15:30 local time.  Teams may set different coverage hours for customer support, fulfilment, and incident response.  Overtime or additional hours require advance manager approval, except in emergencies.  Employees must record time where required by local law or team procedure. Employees must take legally required breaks and daily or weekly rest periods. Managers are responsible for monitoring workload and preventing sustained excessive hours. 4.2 Hybrid and remote work

Eligible roles may use hybrid work under the applicable Hybrid Working Standard HR-014 and local arrangements. Approval is based on role requirements, team coverage, performance, security, and local tax or employment restrictions. Remote employees must:  Work from an approved location recorded in PeopleHub.  Maintain reliable internet access and a suitable, safe workspace.  Protect screens, documents, devices, and calls from unauthorised access.  Attend required office, team, training, or customer meetings.  Obtain approval before working from another country. Working outside the employing country for more than 10 business days in a calendar year requires review by People Operations and Global Mobility before travel. 4.3 Attendance and absence Employees must notify their manager as soon as possible, normally before their scheduled start time, when they cannot work. Absence records and medical documentation must be submitted through PeopleHub in accordance with local law. Managers should contact People Operations when:  Absence lasts more than three consecutive working days.  A pattern of repeated short-term absence is identified.  Workplace adjustments or a phased return may be required.  An employee is absent without notification for one working day. IronStore handles health information as confidential special-category data and limits access to authorised personnel. 5. Leave and Time Off Leave entitlements are governed by the employment contract and local law. PeopleHub is the system of record for requests and balances. 5.1 Annual leave Employees should request annual leave at least 10 calendar days in advance through PeopleHub. Managers should respond within

are governed by the employment contract and local law. PeopleHub is the system of record for requests and balances. 5.1 Annual leave Employees should request annual leave at least 10 calendar days in advance through PeopleHub. Managers should respond within five business days and must consider operational coverage fairly. Employees should not book non-refundable travel until leave is approved. Leave carry-over, minimum usage, and expiry rules differ by country. The relevant country addendum applies. 5.2 Public holidays and other leave

Public holidays follow the employee’s employing entity and approved work location. Statutory leave may include parental, family, bereavement, sick, civic, and other protected leave. Employees should contact their People Partner before taking statutory or extended leave so that documentation, pay, benefits, and return-to-work arrangements can be confirmed. 5.3 Family and personal circumstances IronStore seeks to support employees with caring responsibilities, disability, pregnancy, or other significant personal circumstances. Reasonable adjustments may include changes to working hours, equipment, duties, or location, subject to operational feasibility and local requirements. Requests should be discussed with the manager and People Partner. Medical information should be provided only through approved confidential channels. 6. Pay, Expenses, and Benefits 6.1 Payroll Salary is paid monthly to the bank account registered in PeopleHub. Payroll cut-off is normally the 15th calendar day of each month. Changes submitted after cut-off may be processed in the following pay cycle. Employees must check payslips and report suspected errors to Payroll Operations within 30 days. IronStore may correct overpayments in accordance with local law and agreed repayment arrangements. 6.2 Business expenses Reasonable, necessary business expenses must be submitted in SpendFlow within 30 days of the transaction. Receipts are required for expenses over €25, unless local rules require receipts at a lower threshold. Prior approval is required for:  Travel or accommodation expected to exceed €500.  Customer or supplier hospitality above €75 per person.  Equipment or subscriptions above the team’s delegated budget.  Any expense involving a government official. Expenses must be accurate

is required for:  Travel or accommodation expected to exceed €500.  Customer or supplier hospitality above €75 per person.  Equipment or subscriptions above the team’s delegated budget.  Any expense involving a government official. Expenses must be accurate and must not be split to avoid approval thresholds. Personal purchases are not reimbursable unless explicitly authorised. 6.3 Benefits Benefits vary by employing entity and may include pension contributions, health coverage, employee discounts, wellbeing support, and income protection. Current eligibility and enrolment information is available in PeopleHub. Employees must notify People Operations of relevant changes, such as a change in dependants or address. 7. Information Security, Privacy, and Company Property

Employees are responsible for protecting IronStore data, customer information, and company equipment. Required practices include:  Use IronID multi-factor authentication for company systems.  Store work files in approved services such as IronDrive and Confluence.  Do not share passwords, tokens, or access badges.  Use company-managed devices for customer, payment, employee, and operational data.  Lock screens when unattended and report lost devices immediately.  Check unexpected links, invoices, and payment requests before acting.  Complete annual security and privacy training by the assigned deadline. Suspected phishing, data loss, unauthorised access, or accidental disclosure must be reported immediately through SecurityHub or the 24-hour on-call number listed in the Service Portal. Do not attempt to conceal or independently investigate an incident. IronStore processes personal data under applicable privacy laws, including the GDPR where relevant. Employees may access personal data only when required for their role and must follow retention and deletion instructions. Company equipment remains IronStore property. On transfer or termination, all equipment, records, access cards, and confidential materials must be returned by the date specified by IT or People Operations. 8. Conflicts, Gifts, and Business Integrity Employees must act in IronStore’s interests and disclose actual or potential conflicts to their manager and Compliance. Employees may accept modest, infrequent business hospitality when it is lawful, transparent, and not intended to influence a decision. Gifts or hospitality valued above €50 require manager approval and entry in the Gifts and Hospitality Register. Gifts from suppliers involved in a current tender or contract

hospitality when it is lawful, transparent, and not intended to influence a decision. Gifts or hospitality valued above €50 require manager approval and entry in the Gifts and Hospitality Register. Gifts from suppliers involved in a current tender or contract negotiation must normally be declined. The following are prohibited:  Bribery, facilitation payments, kickbacks, or secret commissions.  Falsifying records, invoices, performance data, or customer information.  Using confidential company information for personal benefit.  Retaliating against someone who raises a good-faith concern. Concerns may be reported through the Speak Up Line, anonymously where legally available. 9. Performance, Learning, and Development Employees receive role objectives through PerformTrack. Managers should provide regular feedback and hold at least quarterly check-ins. Annual reviews normally close in January for the preceding performance year.

Employees are expected to:  Complete mandatory compliance, security, and safety training on time.  Maintain skills relevant to their role.  Discuss development goals during quarterly check-ins.  Participate in improvement plans where performance does not meet expectations. Performance concerns should be addressed promptly, fairly, and with documented expectations, support, and review dates. Formal processes must follow local law and any applicable collective agreement. 10. Health, Safety, and Wellbeing IronStore provides a safe working environment and requires employees to follow site-specific safety instructions. Employees must:  Complete required workplace or warehouse induction before starting relevant work.  Use protective equipment and follow manual-handling procedures.  Report hazards, injuries, near misses, and unsafe behaviour through SafeTrack.  Follow emergency, evacuation, fire, and first-aid instructions.  Never disable safety controls or operate equipment without authorisation. Work-related injuries must be reported to the manager immediately and recorded before the end of the shift where possible. Mental health support is available through the Employee Assistance Programme, listed in PeopleHub. 11. Leaving IronStore Resignation must be submitted in writing to the manager and People Operations. Notice periods follow the employment contract and local law. Before the final working day, employees must:  Complete knowledge transfer and return company property.  Close or transfer open work in approved systems.  Submit outstanding expenses and timesheets.  Remove company data from personal devices.  Attend an exit discussion where requested. System access may be withdrawn before the final day based on security, role, or business requirements.

System access may be withdrawn before the final day based on security, role, or business requirements. Post-employment confidentiality obligations continue after departure. 12. Roles and Responsibilities  Employees: Follow this handbook, local policies, security requirements, and lawful instructions.

 Managers: Apply standards consistently, approve requests promptly, support wellbeing, and escalate issues.  People Partners: Advise on employment matters, workplace concerns, leave, adjustments, and formal processes.  People Operations: Maintain records, policies, payroll coordination, and employee support channels.  Information Security and Privacy: Manage security controls, incidents, access, and data-protection guidance.  Compliance: Maintain integrity standards, investigations, and the Speak Up process. 13. Leave & Absence Policy Owning area: HR_policies Document owner: People Operations Policy ID: HR-POL-014 Version: 3.0 Last reviewed in August 2026 1. Purpose and Overview This policy explains how IronStore employees request, record, approve, and manage annual leave and other absences. It supports consistent workforce planning while ensuring compliance with applicable employment law in each country where IronStore operates. Local statutory requirements, collective agreements, and employment contracts take precedence over this policy. Employees should contact People Operations if a local rule differs from the process described below. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  All IronStore employees, including permanent, fixed-term, part-time, and probationary employees.  Employees working from IronStore offices, fulfilment sites, customer service centres, and approved remote locations.  Line managers responsible for approving leave or managing attendance.  Agency workers and contractors only where their contract or local agreement expressly adopts these procedures. The policy covers:  Annual or holiday leave.  Public holidays and company closure days.  Sickness absence.  Family, parental, compassionate, and other statutory leave.  Unpaid leave and extended absence.  Return-to-work and absence records. 3. Policy Statement IronStore provides leave in accordance with local law, the employee’s contract, and approved company benefits. Employees are expected to take their full statutory annual leave entitlement unless local law permits a lawful carryover or other arrangement.

Leave must be requested in advance through PeopleHub, IronStore’s HR system. Leave is not confirmed until approved by the employee’s line manager, except where an absence is unexpected or legally protected. It may vary by:  Country of employment.  Contractual working hours and working pattern.  Length of service.  Collective agreement or local benefit scheme. Part-time employees receive a pro-rated entitlement where applicable. Public holidays are handled according to the employee’s work location and local law. The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December, unless a local entity has an approved alternative. 4.2 Request and Approval Employees should submit annual leave requests through PeopleHub:  At least 10 calendar days before leave of one to five working days.  At least 20 calendar days before leave exceeding five working days.  As early as possible for peak periods, including July–August, year-end, and major local holidays. Managers should respond within five working days. Approval depends on operational coverage, customer commitments, fulfilment schedules, and previously approved leave.

People Operations will issue reminders during the year. Employees and managers remain jointly responsible for preventing excessive balances. 4.4 Cancelling or Changing Leave Employees should amend or cancel approved leave in PeopleHub before the scheduled start date. Changes are subject to manager approval. IronStore may cancel approved leave only for significant and unforeseen operational reasons. The manager must consult the employee, provide reasonable notice where possible, and reimburse or address unavoidable costs where required by local law. 5. Public Holidays and Company Closure Public holidays are determined by the employee’s official work location. Employees working across borders must confirm the applicable calendar with People Operations. IronStore may designate limited company closure days, such as 24 December through 31 December, for selected offices or teams. Fulfilment, customer service, technology operations, and other continuous-service teams may follow rota arrangements instead of office closure dates. 6. Sickness Absence Employees who cannot work because of illness or injury must notify their manager and record the absence in PeopleHub:  Before their scheduled start time, where reasonably possible.

 By telephone or the approved team channel if they cannot access PeopleHub.  With an expected duration and suitable contact details, without disclosing unnecessary medical information. People Operations may request an Occupational Health assessment where lawful and proportionate. A manager should hold a brief welfare check after approximately five working days, then agree an appropriate contact schedule. Contact must be supportive and must not pressure the employee to return before medically fit. For absence continuing beyond 28 calendar days, People Operations will coordinate a formal case review covering:  Expected timescales and relevant documentation.  Workplace adjustments or phased return options.  Pay, benefits, and statutory reporting.  Any legal or occupational health requirements. 7. Family and Other Statutory Leave IronStore provides statutory and contractual leave available in the employee’s country, including:  Maternity, pregnancy-related, adoption, and parental leave.  Paternity or partner leave.  Carer’s or dependants’ leave.  Bereavement or compassionate leave.  Time off for medical appointments where legally protected.  Jury service, civic duties, military

employee’s country, including:  Maternity, pregnancy-related, adoption, and parental leave.  Paternity or partner leave.  Carer’s or dependants’ leave.  Bereavement or compassionate leave.  Time off for medical appointments where legally protected.  Jury service, civic duties, military obligations, or other statutory absence. Employees should notify their manager and People Operations as early as practicable. Some leave types require formal notice, supporting documents, or a prescribed application form. Requests are handled sensitively. Evidence should be requested only where necessary. 8. Approval requires the line manager and People Operations. Requests exceeding 20 working days also require approval from the relevant department director. Before approval, People Operations will explain effects on salary, benefits, pension or social insurance, holiday accrual, and service dates. Unpaid leave must not be used to conceal sickness absence or work for a competitor. 9. Recording, Pay, and Privacy PeopleHub is the official record for leave and absence. Managers must approve or reject requests promptly and ensure team calendars are accurate. People Operations may correct records where supporting evidence confirms an error. Absence information is personal data. IronStore processes it only for employment administration, legal compliance, health and safety, workforce planning, and related legitimate purposes. Access is restricted by role and retained according to the HR Records Retention Standard (HR-STD-006). 10. Return to Work Following sickness absence, the employee should complete a return-to-work check-in with their manager within three working days. The discussion should cover:  Fitness

Return to Work Following sickness absence, the employee should complete a return-to-work check-in with their manager within three working days. The discussion should cover:  Fitness to resume normal duties.  Any temporary adjustments or support.  Outstanding work and priorities.  Whether further People Operations involvement is needed. A phased return may be agreed with medical or Occupational Health input. Adjustments must be documented in PeopleHub or the approved case-management record and reviewed by the agreed date. 11. Roles and Responsibilities

Remote Work Policy Document owner: HR_policies Policy ID: HR-REM-001 Version: 3.0 Last reviewed: August 2026 Applies to: IronStore employees and long-term contractors in Europe 1. Purpose and Overview IronStore supports remote and hybrid working where the arrangement is compatible with the role, customer commitments, operational requirements, and applicable employment law. The policy is intended to provide flexibility while maintaining service quality, information security, collaboration, and a consistent employee experience across European locations. Remote work is a working arrangement, not an employee entitlement. Approval depends on business needs, role requirements, individual performance, and the ability to work securely from an approved location. The employee’s employment contract, local law, and any country-specific addendum take precedence where requirements differ. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  Permanent and fixed-term employees working from IronStore offices or approved remote locations.  Long-term contractors where their contract incorporates IronStore workplace policies.  Employees working in customer service, fulfilment support, merchandising, technology, finance, HR, and corporate functions.  Remote work performed within the employee’s approved employing country. This policy does not normally cover:  Warehouse, delivery, retail-support, or other roles requiring physical presence.  Temporary work-from-home arrangements during illness or medical leave.  Business travel, relocation, or working from another country.  Employees subject to a separate local remote-work agreement. Working outside the employee’s approved country requires prior approval under the International Work from Abroad Procedure (HR-REM-004). 3. Policy Statement 3.1 Working Models

IronStore uses the following working models:  Office-based: Work is primarily performed at an assigned IronStore location.  Hybrid: Work is performed at an IronStore location on designated days and remotely on other working days.  Remote-first: Work is normally performed remotely, with attendance required for team events, planning sessions, training, or other business needs. The hiring manager and People Partner confirm the working model during recruitment or internal transfer. The model is recorded in Workday and reviewed at least annually. Most eligible hybrid employees are expected to attend their designated office an average of two days per week. Teams may set a higher attendance requirement during peak trading periods, operational changes, or major projects. Managers must provide reasonable notice, normally at least five working days, except for urgent business requirements. 3.2 Eligibility and Approval Employees may request remote or hybrid work after completing their probationary period, unless an earlier arrangement is approved in writing. Approval requires: 1. A request submitted through the Workday Flexible Work Request form. 2. Manager assessment of role suitability, performance, team coverage, and customer impact. 3. Review by the relevant People Partner. 4. Country-specific review where required by local employment law. 5. Written confirmation of the approved schedule, location, duration, and review date. Managers should respond within 15 calendar days. An approval may be permanent, time-limited, or subject to a trial period of up to three months. Requests may be declined where remote work would create unacceptable operational, security, collaboration, performance, or cost risks. The

Requests may be declined where remote work would create unacceptable operational, security, collaboration, performance, or cost risks. The manager must document the reason and discuss alternatives with the employee. 3.3 Approved Work Location The approved remote location must:  Be within the employee’s employing country.  Provide a safe, suitable, and reasonably private working environment.  Have reliable internet access and sufficient space for company equipment.  Support confidentiality, video meetings, and uninterrupted work.  Be recorded in Workday and kept current. Employees must notify their manager and People Operations before changing their regular remote location. Remote work from cafés, public transport, shared accommodation, or public co-working spaces is permitted only for low-risk activities. Confidential discussions, customer data, payment information, and restricted documents must not be accessed or discussed in locations where they may be overheard or viewed. 3.4 Working Hours and Availability Employees must work the hours stated in their contract and comply with local working-time requirements. Unless an alternative schedule is approved, employees should be available during their team’s core hours:  Core hours: 10:00–15:00 local time, Monday to Friday.  Customer and operational teams: Hours specified by the team rota.  Cross-border teams: Overlap periods agreed by the manager and recorded in the team handbook. Employees must keep their status accurate in Microsoft Teams, attend required meetings, and respond to normal business messages within one working day. Calendar blocks should indicate focus time, breaks, annual leave, and other periods of unavailability. Managers should assess outcomes rather than online presence. Monitoring employees through continuous webcam use, keystroke tracking, or unapproved surveillance tools is not permitted. 3.5 Attendance and Collaboration Remote employees are expected to participate fully in team activities. Teams may require attendance at:  Quarterly planning and performance meetings.  Onboarding, training, workshops, and compliance sessions.  Critical incident reviews or operational meetings.  Customer, supplier, or leadership events.  Office days published in the team calendar. Employees who cannot attend must notify the organiser and review the available notes or recording. 3.6 Equipment, Expenses, and Office Setup IronStore provides standard equipment based on role requirements. All equipment remains IronStore property and must be returned when requested or when employment ends. Employees must not install unauthorised software or allow household members to use company devices. IronStore does not normally reimburse furniture, home internet, electricity, heating, or rent unless required by local law or a written country addendum. Approved business travel to an IronStore office is reimbursed under the Business Travel and Expenses Policy (FIN-EXP-002). Equipment purchases require manager approval before ordering through Coupa. Employees should report workstation or ergonomic concerns to Workplace Services. A workplace assessment may be arranged through the local occupational health provider. 3.7 Information Security and Privacy Remote employees must comply with the Information Security Policy (SEC-001) and the following minimum controls:  Use only IronStore-managed devices for company work.  Connect through the IronStore VPN when accessing restricted systems.  Use multi-factor authentication through Microsoft Entra ID.  Lock the screen whenever leaving the workstation.  Store business files in approved services, including OneDrive, SharePoint, and Confluence.  Avoid printing confidential information; securely destroy any approved printouts.  Use a privacy screen when working in public or shared areas.  Never forward company data to personal email or storage accounts.  Report suspected loss, phishing, or unauthorised access immediately through the ServiceNow Security Incident form. They must report accidents, work-related injuries, or unsafe conditions to their manager and People Operations as soon as possible. Remote workers should:  Take regular screen breaks and vary working posture.  Keep cables and equipment clear of walkways.  Use suitable lighting and ventilation.  Separate work and personal time where practical.  Raise workload, isolation, or wellbeing concerns early.
