IT Security Policy Owning area: IT Policy owner: Director of Information Security Document ID: ITS-POL-001 Version: 4.0 Last reviewed: August 2026 Next scheduled review: August 2027 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines the minimum security requirements for IronStore’s information systems, devices, applications, and data. IronStore operates across Europe and processes customer, employee, supplier, payment, and operational information. Security controls must protect confidentiality, integrity, availability, and legal compliance. The policy supports IronStore’s obligations under applicable European data protection and cybersecurity requirements, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the NIS2 Directive where applicable, and local employment and regulatory requirements. It applies a risk-based approach: higher-risk systems and data require stronger controls, closer monitoring, and more frequent review. All employees, contractors, temporary workers, and third parties with access to IronStore resources must comply with this policy. Failure to comply may result in access removal, disciplinary action, contract termination, or legal action. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  IronStore corporate offices, warehouses, fulfilment sites, and remote working environments.  Company-managed laptops, mobile devices, servers, network equipment, and storage.  Cloud services, including Microsoft 365, Azure, Shopify Plus, Salesforce, Jira, and Snowflake.  Customer, employee, supplier, financial, payment, product, and operational data.  Employees, contractors, agency workers, service providers, and approved business partners.  Systems developed, operated, or procured by IronStore, including mobile applications and e-commerce platforms. Personal devices may access IronStore systems only through an approved Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) arrangement and must meet the requirements in the Device Standard.

partners.  Systems developed, operated, or procured by IronStore, including mobile applications and e-commerce platforms. Personal devices may access IronStore systems only through an approved Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) arrangement and must meet the requirements in the Device Standard. 3. Policy Statement and Procedures 3.1 Information Classification

Information owners must classify data when it is created or received. The following classifications apply:  Public: Approved for unrestricted external release, such as published product descriptions.  Internal: Routine business information intended for IronStore personnel.  Confidential: Information that could cause material harm if disclosed, including contracts, pricing plans, source code, and supplier terms.  Restricted: Highly sensitive information requiring enhanced controls, including payment-related data, identity documents, authentication secrets, health information, and unmasked customer records. Requirements:  Restricted data must be encrypted in transit and at rest.  Confidential and Restricted data must not be sent to personal email, consumer file-sharing services, or unapproved AI or productivity tools.  Access must be granted on a least-privilege and need-to-know basis.  Data owners must review access to Restricted repositories at least quarterly.  Suspected loss or unauthorised disclosure must be reported to the Security Operations mailbox immediately. 3.2 Identity and Access Management IronStore uses Microsoft Entra ID as the primary identity provider and requires centralised authentication wherever technically possible.  Each individual must use a unique IronStore account. Shared accounts are prohibited unless approved by Information Security.  Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for Microsoft 365, VPN, cloud consoles, administrative tools, and production systems.  Phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO2 security keys or passkeys, is required for privileged administrators and payment-platform administrators.  Access requests must be approved by the user’s line manager and the relevant system owner.  Privileged access requires an additional approval from the IT Security Manager.

security keys or passkeys, is required for privileged administrators and payment-platform administrators.  Access requests must be approved by the user’s line manager and the relevant system owner.  Privileged access requires an additional approval from the IT Security Manager.  Access must be removed within four hours of a confirmed termination and by the end of the worker’s last day for planned departures.  Role changes must trigger an access review within five business days.  Dormant accounts are disabled after 45 days unless the system owner documents a business reason.  Passwords must be unique, stored only in the approved password manager, and never shared through chat or email.  Service accounts must have a named owner, documented purpose, restricted permissions, and secrets rotated at least every 180 days. Quarterly, system owners must certify access to critical systems, including the order management platform, warehouse management system, ERP, customer service platform, and payment administration consoles. 3.3 Endpoint and Mobile Security

All company-managed endpoints must be enrolled in Microsoft Intune and protected by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Minimum requirements include:  Automatic operating system and application updates.  Full-disk encryption using BitLocker or an approved equivalent.  Screen lock after a maximum of 10 minutes of inactivity.  Endpoint detection and response enabled and reporting to the Security Operations Centre (SOC).  Local administrator rights removed unless a documented exception is approved.  Approved endpoint firewall and anti-malware controls enabled.  Corporate data stored only in approved locations, such as OneDrive, SharePoint, or managed application storage. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the Service Desk within one hour of discovery. IT may remotely lock or wipe the device. Employees must not disable security software, install unapproved software, or connect unknown USB devices to company equipment. Remote work must use a private, access-controlled network. Public Wi-Fi may be used only with the IronStore VPN or an approved zero-trust connection. Confidential discussions must not take place where unauthorised people can overhear them. 3.4 Network, Cloud, and Application Security The Infrastructure team must maintain separate development, test, and production environments. Production access must be restricted, logged, and reviewed.  Internet-facing services must be protected by approved web application firewall and distributed denial-of-service controls.  Administrative interfaces must not be directly exposed to the public internet.  Network security groups and firewall rules require documented owners and annual review.  Critical cloud services must use central logging, MFA, encryption, and region-appropriate data residency

controls.  Administrative interfaces must not be directly exposed to the public internet.  Network security groups and firewall rules require documented owners and annual review.  Critical cloud services must use central logging, MFA, encryption, and region-appropriate data residency settings.  Production secrets must be stored in Azure Key Vault or another approved secrets-management service.  Customer payment data must be processed through approved payment service providers. IronStore systems must not store full card numbers or CVV data.  Source code must be stored in IronStore GitHub Enterprise repositories with branch protection and mandatory peer review.  High-risk code changes require security review before production deployment.  Vulnerability scanning must run at least weekly for internet-facing assets and before major releases. Development teams must use synthetic or masked data in non-production environments. Production data may be copied to test systems only with written approval from the system owner, Data Protection Officer, and Security Architecture lead.

3.5 Vulnerability and Patch Management IT Security maintains the central asset and vulnerability register. Asset owners are responsible for remediation within these limits:  Critical vulnerabilities with known exploitation: mitigation within 24 hours and remediation within seven days.  Other Critical vulnerabilities: remediation within 14 days.  High vulnerabilities: remediation within 30 days.  Medium vulnerabilities: remediation within 90 days.  Low vulnerabilities: address during normal maintenance planning. Where remediation is not possible, the owner must document compensating controls, business impact, and a target date. Exceptions require approval from the Director of Information Security and expire after 90 days unless renewed. Unsupported operating systems, applications, and network devices must not be used in production unless an approved exception and replacement plan exist. 3.6 Logging, Monitoring, and Security Events Security-relevant events must be recorded centrally in Microsoft Sentinel or an approved equivalent. Critical systems must log authentication, privilege changes, configuration changes, administrative actions, and data export events.  Logs must use synchronised time sources.  Security logs must be retained for at least 12 months, subject to legal and privacy requirements.  Restricted-data access logs must be protected from alteration.  The SOC monitors alerts during business hours and maintains an on-call escalation rota for critical events.  High-severity alerts must be triaged within 30 minutes.  Log access is limited to authorised IT Security personnel and approved investigators. Employees must report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorised access, data loss, or unusual system behaviour through the Service Desk portal, the “Report Phishing”

be triaged within 30 minutes.  Log access is limited to authorised IT Security personnel and approved investigators. Employees must report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorised access, data loss, or unusual system behaviour through the Service Desk portal, the “Report Phishing” button, or the 24-hour security contact number listed on the intranet. They must not investigate beyond basic safe actions or delete evidence. 3.7 Incident Response The Incident Response Plan defines the response process. All suspected incidents are recorded in ServiceNow with a severity, owner, timeline, and affected assets. Response stages are: 1. Identify and contain: Confirm the event, isolate affected accounts or devices, and preserve evidence. 2. Assess: Determine affected systems, data, jurisdictions, and business impact. 3. Eradicate and recover: Remove the cause, restore services, and validate system security.

4. Notify and review: Inform management, Legal, Privacy, insurers, regulators, customers, or law enforcement where required. Potential personal data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Officer immediately and no later than two hours after discovery. The DPO determines whether regulatory notification is required. Employees must not contact regulators, customers, or media about a security incident unless authorised. A post-incident review must be completed within ten business days for High and Critical incidents. Actions are tracked to closure by the Security Governance team. 3.8 Backup, Continuity, and Recovery Critical business services, including checkout, order management, fulfilment, customer service, ERP, and identity services, must have documented recovery requirements.  Critical production data must be backed up daily, with more frequent replication where defined by the service owner.  Backups must be encrypted, access-controlled, and protected against deletion or ransomware.  At least one backup copy must be logically or physically separated from the production environment.  Restore tests must be completed quarterly for Tier 1 systems and annually for other critical systems.  Recovery results and unresolved gaps must be reported to the IT Risk Committee. Business owners must maintain manual workarounds for essential fulfilment, customer support, and payment reconciliation activities. 3.9 Third-Party Security Procurement and the system owner must complete a security and privacy assessment before a supplier receives Confidential or Restricted data or connects to IronStore systems. Contracts must address:  Security controls and incident notification.  Data processing responsibilities and sub-processors.  Access limitation and authentication. 

complete a security and privacy assessment before a supplier receives Confidential or Restricted data or connects to IronStore systems. Contracts must address:  Security controls and incident notification.  Data processing responsibilities and sub-processors.  Access limitation and authentication.  Data location, retention, deletion, and return.  Audit rights or equivalent assurance reports.  Exit arrangements and secure transfer of data. Critical suppliers are reviewed annually. Supplier access must be time-limited, individually assigned, MFA-protected, and removed when the engagement ends. 3.10 Security Awareness All personnel must complete security and privacy training within 30 days of joining IronStore and annually thereafter. Additional training is required for developers, privileged administrators, warehouse technology users, customer

service teams, and personnel handling Restricted data. IronStore may conduct simulated phishing exercises. Personnel who fail a simulation may be assigned targeted training. Repeated unsafe behaviour is escalated to the individual’s manager. 4. Roles and Responsibilities  Board and Executive Committee: Set risk appetite and receive material security reporting.  Director of Information Security: Own this policy, approve security standards, and escalate significant risks.  Security Operations Centre: Monitor alerts, coordinate incident response, and maintain security tooling.  IT Infrastructure: Operate identity, endpoint, network, backup, and cloud controls.  System and Data Owners: Approve access, classify information, manage risks, and maintain recovery requirements.  Data Protection Officer: Advise on GDPR, breach assessment, data subject rights, and privacy impact assessments.  Procurement and Legal: Ensure supplier contracts include appropriate security and privacy terms.  Managers: Confirm staff access, training, and compliance for their teams.  All personnel: Protect credentials, follow procedures, and report security concerns promptly. 5. Password & Access Management Policy Policy ID: IT-SEC-04 Owning area: IT Policy owner: Head of Infrastructure & Security Version: 4.0 Last reviewed: August 2026 Applies to: IronStore GmbH and all European subsidiaries Purpose / Overview This policy defines how IronStore creates, manages, reviews, and removes access to company systems and information. Its purpose is to reduce the risk of account compromise, unauthorised access, data loss, and operational disruption. Access must be based on business need, limited to the minimum required level, and removed promptly when no longer required. IronStore uses central identity management, multi-factor authentication (MFA), role-based access controls, and periodic access reviews to support this policy. Scope This policy applies to:  Employees, temporary staff, contractors, consultants, interns, and agency workers.  Corporate accounts, privileged accounts, service accounts, and shared technical accounts.  Company-managed laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops, and approved personal devices used for work.  Systems operated by IronStore or on its behalf, including:  Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365.  Workday, SAP S/4HANA, and finance applications.  Shopify Plus, warehouse management systems, and logistics platforms.  AWS, Azure, GitHub Enterprise, Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce.  Customer support, marketing, payment, and analytics platforms.  Third-party access to IronStore systems or data. This policy does not replace system-specific security requirements. Where requirements conflict, the stricter requirement applies unless the CISO approves an exception. Policy Statement and Procedures 1. Account and Identity Standards

system-specific security requirements. Where requirements conflict, the stricter requirement applies unless the CISO approves an exception. Policy Statement and Procedures 1. Account and Identity Standards

Each person must use an individual IronStore account. Accounts must not be shared, transferred, or used by another person.  Usernames follow the format firstname.lastname@ironstore.eu.  HR must create or update the employee record before IT provisions access.  Identity records must include the person’s legal name, manager, department, employment status, and location.  Accounts must be linked to a unique employee or contractor identifier.  Personal email addresses must not be used for company accounts.  Local administrator rights are prohibited unless approved under the Privileged Access Standard.  Dormant accounts are disabled after 30 days without successful authentication.  Disabled accounts are deleted or archived after 90 days, subject to legal hold and retention requirements. IT Service Desk may create a temporary account only where the request includes a named owner, business reason, expiry date, and approving manager. 2. Password Requirements Passwords must be resistant to guessing and must not be reused across company and personal services. For systems that support modern authentication:  Passwords must be at least 14 characters long.  Passphrases of four or more unrelated words are recommended.  Passwords must not contain the user’s name, username, company name, product names, or common seasonal terms.  Passwords must not appear in the 10,000 most commonly used passwords or known breach lists.  Password managers approved by IT, currently 1Password Business, must be used for storing corporate credentials.  Passwords must not be stored in browsers, spreadsheets, tickets, chat messages, or unencrypted files.  Passwords

commonly used passwords or known breach lists.  Password managers approved by IT, currently 1Password Business, must be used for storing corporate credentials.  Passwords must not be stored in browsers, spreadsheets, tickets, chat messages, or unencrypted files.  Passwords must not be sent by email or communicated verbally. Routine password changes are not required for standard accounts when MFA and risk-based controls are enabled. A password must be changed immediately if:  The account may have been compromised.  The password was disclosed, reused, or entered into an unapproved site.  Security Operations instructs the user to change it.  The system does not support MFA or is identified as high risk. Systems that cannot support MFA must enforce a minimum 16-character password and a maximum password age of 180 days. Exceptions require written approval from the CISO. 3. Multi-Factor Authentication

MFA is mandatory for all externally accessible company systems and all administrative access.  The preferred method is a FIDO2 security key or passkey.  Authenticator applications using number matching are permitted.  SMS may be used only as a temporary recovery method or where no stronger method is supported.  Email-based one-time codes are not an approved primary MFA method.  At least two MFA methods must be registered for employees with privileged or business-critical access.  Recovery codes must be stored in the approved password manager or a secured physical location.  Users must never approve an unexpected MFA prompt.  Repeated unexpected prompts must be reported to the Service Desk or Security Operations immediately. MFA resets require identity verification through the Service Desk. For privileged users, the reset must be approved by the user’s manager or the on-call Security Operations lead. 4. Access Requests and Approval Access is granted through the IronStore ServiceNow request catalogue. Requests must specify:  The system, role, and access level requested.  Business purpose and expected duration.  The user’s manager and cost centre.  Any customer, payment, production, or personal-data access involved. Standard access is approved by the line manager and the system owner. Sensitive or privileged access additionally requires approval from the relevant data owner. Production access, payment-system access, and access to customer exports require approval from both the system owner and the Head of Infrastructure & Security. IT fulfils approved requests through Microsoft Entra ID groups, application roles, or

from the relevant data owner. Production access, payment-system access, and access to customer exports require approval from both the system owner and the Head of Infrastructure & Security. IT fulfils approved requests through Microsoft Entra ID groups, application roles, or the CyberArk Privilege Cloud platform. Direct permissions should not be assigned unless the system cannot support group-based access. Target fulfilment times are:  Standard employee access: one business day.  New starter access: by 09:00 local time on the start date, if requested at least three business days in advance.  Privileged or production access: two business days after all approvals are complete.  Urgent access: only through the emergency access process. 5. Joiner, Mover, and Leaver Controls HR is responsible for providing timely employment-status information to IT and the employee’s manager. Joiners  HR submits the starter record at least three business days before the start date.  The manager requests only the access required for the employee’s initial duties.

 Accounts remain disabled until the start date unless an earlier date is approved by HR and IT.  New users must complete security awareness training within 30 days. Movers  Managers must review access when an employee changes role, department, country, or reporting line.  Access not required for the new role must be removed within one business day of the change.  A new role must not be used to retain incompatible financial or operational permissions.  System owners must resolve conflicting access identified by the quarterly review. Leavers  Involuntary termination: accounts, sessions, tokens, VPN access, and privileged credentials are disabled at the agreed termination time.  Planned departure: access is removed no later than the employee’s final working day.  Company devices, security keys, and access badges must be returned.  Shared mailbox and document ownership must be transferred to the manager.  Service accounts, API keys, and automation owned by the leaver must be reassigned or rotated. 6. Purpose and Overview This workflow defines how IronStore contracts must be requested, reviewed, approved, signed, stored, and monitored. It is intended to ensure that contracts are commercially sound, legally compliant, accurately recorded, and approved by the appropriate budget and risk owners. The workflow applies to supplier, logistics, technology, marketing, employment-related commercial, marketplace, consulting, real estate, and other business agreements. No employee may commit IronStore to contractual obligations outside this process. Contracts must be handled through the designated systems and approval chains. Email approval alone is not sufficient unless specifically permitted under this document. 2. Scope This workflow applies to:  New contracts, statements of work, order forms, amendments, renewals, and termination agreements.  Contracts with suppliers, service providers, brands, agencies, landlords, technology vendors, and business partners.  Agreements involving IronStore entities in the EU, EEA, United Kingdom, or Switzerland.  Contracts that process personal data, create intellectual property obligations, or involve customer-facing services.  Purchases and commitments with a total expected value of €5,000 or more, including committed renewal periods. The workflow does not replace specialist review required for:  Employment contracts and employee relations matters.  Product safety, customs, tax, or regulated product assessments.  Information security assessments for technology or data-processing services.  Real estate transactions or material financing arrangements.

Data Privacy & GDPR Compliance Policy Owning area: Legal_Terms Policy ID: LEG-PRV-001 Version: 4.2 Last reviewed: August 2026 Policy owner: Group Data Protection Officer (DPO) 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines how IronStore collects, uses, stores, shares, and protects personal data in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), applicable national privacy laws, and contractual obligations. IronStore sells consumer products across Europe, including electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and related categories. The policy applies to customer, employee, supplier, courier, marketplace, and website visitor data processed through IronStore systems or on its behalf. Compliance is mandatory. Business teams must involve Legal_Terms before launching processing activities that create new privacy risks, introduce new tracking technologies, or materially change how personal data is used. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  IronStore GmbH and all European subsidiaries and branches.  Employees, temporary workers, contractors, and approved service providers.  Customer-facing websites, mobile applications, marketplaces, customer service channels, and fulfilment operations.  Personal data in production, test, support, analytics, backup, and paper environments.  Processing performed by third parties under an IronStore contract. The policy covers personal data relating to identified or identifiable individuals. Anonymous information, which cannot reasonably be linked to an individual, is outside the GDPR but must still be handled securely. 3. Policy Statement and Procedures 3.1 Core Privacy Principles IronStore processes personal data according to these principles:  Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency: use a valid legal basis and provide clear notices.  Purpose limitation: use

must still be handled securely. 3. Policy Statement and Procedures 3.1 Core Privacy Principles IronStore processes personal data according to these principles:  Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency: use a valid legal basis and provide clear notices.  Purpose limitation: use data only for defined, compatible business purposes.

 Data minimisation: collect only information necessary for the stated purpose.  Accuracy: enable correction and remove data that is no longer reliable.  Storage limitation: retain data only for approved periods.  Integrity and confidentiality: protect data against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure.  Accountability: maintain evidence of decisions, controls, training, and reviews. No team may use customer data for a new purpose merely because the data is already available in Salesforce, Snowflake, Magento, or another approved system. 3.2 Lawful Basis and Transparency The responsible business owner must document the lawful basis before processing begins. Approved bases include:  Contract: order fulfilment, payment processing, delivery, returns, and customer account administration.  Legal obligation: tax, accounting, product safety, fraud prevention, and regulatory reporting.  Legitimate interests: service security, limited operational analytics, debt recovery, and carefully assessed business communications.  Consent: optional marketing, non-essential cookies, personalised advertising, and certain profiling activities.  Vital interests or public task: only where specifically validated by Legal_Terms. Marketing consent must be recorded in the ConsentHub service, including timestamp, wording presented, channel, country, and withdrawal status. Pre-ticked boxes, bundled consent, and consent obtained through misleading wording are prohibited. Every customer-facing collection point must link to the current Privacy Notice. Material changes require approval from Legal_Terms and, where appropriate, renewed consent. 3.3 Data Collection and Classification Teams must classify information in the IronStore Data Register:  Public: information approved for public release.  Internal: routine business information with limited impact if disclosed.  Confidential: personal data,

and, where appropriate, renewed consent. 3.3 Data Collection and Classification Teams must classify information in the IronStore Data Register:  Public: information approved for public release.  Internal: routine business information with limited impact if disclosed.  Confidential: personal data, commercial information, and customer records.  Restricted: payment data, identity documents, authentication secrets, health information, or high-risk combinations of data. Sensitive or special-category data must not be collected unless expressly required, legally justified, and approved by the DPO. Payment card numbers must not be stored in IronStore applications; payments must use the tokenised Adyen platform. Production personal data must not be copied into development or training environments. Where testing requires realistic records, teams must use synthetic data or an approved anonymisation process. 3.4 Access Control and Security

System owners must apply least-privilege access and review permissions at least quarterly. Access to restricted data requires multi-factor authentication through Microsoft Entra ID and must be logged. Minimum controls include:  Role-based access in Magento Commerce, Salesforce Service Cloud, Snowflake, and warehouse systems.  Encryption in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and encryption at rest for hosted databases.  Endpoint protection and managed device controls through Microsoft Intune.  Central security monitoring in Microsoft Sentinel.  Immediate access removal when employment or supplier access ends.  No transmission of customer files through personal email, consumer file-sharing services, or unapproved messaging applications. Exporting more than 10,000 customer records, or any restricted dataset, requires written approval from the system owner and the DPO or delegated Privacy Counsel. 3.5 Retention and Deletion The approved retention schedule is maintained in LEG-PRV-004 Data Retention Standard. Unless a longer period is required by law, contract, or an active dispute:  Order, invoice, and tax records: 10 years after the relevant financial year.  Customer account data: until account closure, then deleted or anonymised within 90 days.  Customer service cases: 3 years after closure.  Marketing suppression records: retained only to honour opt-out requests.  Delivery and returns records: 3 years after completion.  Web analytics identifiers: 14 months, unless a shorter consent setting applies.  CCTV footage at fulfilment sites: normally 30 days, subject to incident preservation. Deletion jobs run monthly through the Data Lifecycle Manager. Legal holds, fraud investigations, chargebacks, and regulatory requests

analytics identifiers: 14 months, unless a shorter consent setting applies.  CCTV footage at fulfilment sites: normally 30 days, subject to incident preservation. Deletion jobs run monthly through the Data Lifecycle Manager. Legal holds, fraud investigations, chargebacks, and regulatory requests suspend deletion for the affected records. Business owners must document the reason and expected end date. 3.6 Individual Rights Requests Individuals may exercise rights through the privacy form on IronStore.eu, by emailing privacy@ironstore.eu, or through Customer Support. Requests must be recorded in PrivacyDesk and acknowledged within five business days. The Privacy Operations team must: 1. Verify identity using proportionate checks; do not request unnecessary identity documents. 2. Search relevant systems, including CRM, order, marketing, support, and consent records. 3. Consult Legal_Terms where exemptions, third-party data, or complex searches apply.

4. Respond without undue delay and normally within one month. 5. Extend the deadline by up to two additional months only where the request is complex; notify the requester within the first month. 6. Record the outcome, search scope, approvals, and response date. Requests include access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection, and withdrawal of consent. Automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects require a documented human review route. 3.7 Cookies, Tracking, and Profiling Non-essential cookies, advertising pixels, session replay, and similar technologies require prior consent in the CookieHub CMP. Strictly necessary technologies may operate without consent where legally permitted. The Web Product team must:  Maintain an approved tag inventory.  Block unconsented tags before consent is recorded.  Re-scan production websites monthly.  Obtain Privacy Engineering approval before adding a new vendor tag.  Record vendor, purpose, data categories, retention, and transfer location. Personalised recommendations may use purchase and browsing data only for documented purposes. High-impact profiling, sensitive inferences, or combined datasets require a DPIA and DPO approval before deployment. 3.8 Suppliers and International Transfers Procurement must involve Legal_Terms before a supplier receives personal data. Contracts must include appropriate data processing terms, confidentiality, security controls, subprocessor notification, audit rights, deletion or return obligations, and assistance with GDPR rights. The supplier must be listed in the Vendor Privacy Register. Data Processing Agreements are mandatory for processors unless Legal_Terms documents a justified exception. Transfers outside the European Economic Area require an approved mechanism, such as:  An adequacy decision. 

The supplier must be listed in the Vendor Privacy Register. Data Processing Agreements are mandatory for processors unless Legal_Terms documents a justified exception. Transfers outside the European Economic Area require an approved mechanism, such as:  An adequacy decision.  EU Standard Contractual Clauses.  Binding Corporate Rules.  A documented derogation for an occasional, necessary transfer. Legal_Terms must complete a Transfer Impact Assessment where required. Teams may not approve a vendor’s standard international transfer terms without review. 3.9 Data Protection Impact Assessments A DPIA is required before processing likely to create a high risk to individuals, including:

 Large-scale profiling or behavioural advertising.  Systematic monitoring of public areas or workers.  Processing special-category data at scale.  Biometric identification or significant automated decision-making.  Combining datasets from multiple business functions.  A new technology that materially changes the risk profile. The project owner completes the DPIA Template LEG-PRV-006 with Security and Engineering. The DPO approves, rejects, or requires mitigations before go-live. Unresolved high risks must be referred to the relevant supervisory authority where legally required. 3.10 Incidents and Personal Data Breaches Employees must report suspected loss, unauthorised access, misdirected emails, ransomware, or accidental disclosure immediately through security@ironstore.eu and the ServiceNow Security Incident form. Reports should be made within one hour where possible. Security Operations leads containment and evidence preservation. The DPO assesses notification requirements with Legal_Terms:  Supervisory authority notification is targeted within 72 hours of becoming aware of a reportable breach.  Affected individuals are notified without undue delay where the risk is high.  All incidents, including non-reportable events, are recorded in the Breach Register.  Employees must not contact regulators, customers, or media about an incident unless authorised. 3.11 Training and Monitoring All personnel complete privacy and information security training during onboarding and annually thereafter. Customer Support, Marketing, Product, Engineering, HR, and fulfilment managers receive role-specific training. Compliance is monitored through quarterly access reviews, annual supplier assessments, retention-job reports, cookie scans, and internal audits. Repeated non-compliance may result in access restrictions, disciplinary action, contract termination, or escalation to the Executive Risk Committee. 4.

Terms of Service Overview Owning area: Legal_Terms Last reviewed: August 2026 Document ID: LEG-TS-001 Applies to: IronStore websites, mobile applications, customer service channels, and connected marketplace services operating in the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Purpose / Overview This document summarises the rules governing customer use of IronStore services and the purchase of products through IronStore-operated channels. It provides an internal reference for Legal, Customer Operations, Product, Engineering, Finance, and Commercial teams. The approved customer-facing Terms of Service remain the controlling document. This overview explains how those Terms must be maintained, implemented, communicated, and escalated. Teams must not publish alternative wording or make customer commitments that conflict with the approved Terms. This overview does not replace:  Country-specific consumer rights requirements.  Privacy notices or cookie documentation.  Seller agreements or logistics contracts.  Internal information-security, fraud, or payment policies. Customer-facing suspension messages must be factual, proportionate, and limited to the information necessary to protect IronStore’s legitimate interests. 3. Required information includes:  Product name, key characteristics, dimensions, and material where relevant.  Total price, including applicable taxes and mandatory charges.  Delivery costs, estimated delivery timeframe, and delivery restrictions.  Safety warnings, age restrictions, conformity information, and responsible operator details where required.  Seller identity for marketplace products.  Availability status and any purchase quantity limits. Pricing and promotional claims must be supported by evidence in PIMCore or the applicable campaign record. Claims such as “lowest price,” “limited time,” or “number one” require Commercial and Legal approval. If a material pricing or product error is identified before dispatch, Order Operations must pause fulfilment and notify the customer promptly. The customer must be offered the legally required options, including cancellation and refund where applicable. Changes to an already accepted order require Legal review if the change disadvantages the customer. 4. Order Acceptance and Payment An order confirmation acknowledges receipt of the customer’s order. It does not necessarily mean that IronStore has accepted the order where the Terms state that acceptance occurs at dispatch or another defined event. The checkout flow must:  Display the selected products, quantities, total price, delivery charges, and applicable taxes. 

not necessarily mean that IronStore has accepted the order where the Terms state that acceptance occurs at dispatch or another defined event. The checkout flow must:  Display the selected products, quantities, total price, delivery charges, and applicable taxes.  Require an express order action, such as “Pay and place order.”  Allow customers to correct errors before submission.  Provide access to the applicable Terms and privacy information.  Generate an order reference and confirmation email.  Store the accepted Terms version with the order record. Payments are processed through approved providers connected to Adyen and Checkout.com. Teams must not request or store full card numbers outside approved payment systems. Suspected payment irregularities must be routed to Fraud Operations under FRD-04. Refunds normally use the original payment method unless the customer agrees to another method. Finance must investigate unresolved payment or refund exceptions older than five business days.

5. Delivery, Cancellation, and Returns The delivery promise shown at checkout must be based on the fulfilment service level recorded in OMS Atlas. If a delivery is delayed, Customer Operations must provide the customer with an updated estimate and the available legal remedies. Customers may have a statutory right to withdraw from distance contracts. The relevant period, exclusions, return method, and refund process must be stated in the country version of the Terms. Returns processing requirements:  Return requests are logged in ReturnFlow against the order number.  Eligibility is assessed using the applicable territory rules.  Refund decisions are based on receipt, product condition, and statutory rights.  Refunds must not be withheld solely because a customer used a preferred return carrier where the Terms permit another method.  Damaged, unsafe, or incorrectly supplied products are escalated to Quality Operations.  Exclusions for hygiene-sealed, personalised, digital, or perishable products must be legally valid and clearly disclosed. Customer Operations should acknowledge a return or complaint within two business days. Standard refund processing is five business days after the return is approved, subject to payment-provider timelines. 6. Product Defects, Warranties, and Complaints IronStore must distinguish between:  Statutory consumer remedies.  Voluntary manufacturer or IronStore warranties.  Commercial goodwill offers.  Marketplace seller obligations. Agents must not describe a goodwill replacement as a waiver of statutory rights. Defect claims must be recorded in CaseHub with photographs, product identifiers, purchase date, and the remedy offered. Safety complaints, suspected counterfeit products, and repeated

Marketplace seller obligations. Agents must not describe a goodwill replacement as a waiver of statutory rights. Defect claims must be recorded in CaseHub with photographs, product identifiers, purchase date, and the remedy offered. Safety complaints, suspected counterfeit products, and repeated product failures must be escalated within one business day to Product Compliance and the Legal Duty Manager. A product may be temporarily delisted where risk is credible and cannot be mitigated immediately. Formal legal complaints, regulator correspondence, and pre-action letters must be forwarded to Legal Operations on the day received. Customer-facing teams must not speculate on liability or provide settlement commitments without approval. 7. Promotions, Vouchers, and Reviews Every promotion must have a campaign record in PromoDesk containing:

 Campaign owner and approval chain.  Start and end dates.  Eligible products, territories, and customer groups.  Discount calculation and reference-price evidence.  Voucher limits, exclusions, and cancellation rules.  Customer-facing Terms and required disclosures. Promotional Terms require approval from the Commercial owner and Legal_Terms before launch. Technical implementation must be tested in staging, including expired, combined, refunded, and partially used vouchers. Reviews must reflect genuine customer experiences. Moderation may remove content that is unlawful, defamatory, discriminatory, irrelevant, fraudulent, or contains personal data. Negative reviews must not be removed merely because they criticise IronStore or a seller. 8. Changes to the Terms Legal_Terms reviews the master Terms at least annually and whenever there is a material change to law, business model, payment flow, fulfilment model, or marketplace functionality. Change procedure: 1. Business owner submits a change request in Jira project LEGAL, including reason, territories, and implementation date. 2. Legal_Terms prepares revised wording and a change summary. 3. Privacy, Compliance, Product, and Customer Operations review impacts where applicable. 4. The Head of Legal approves material changes; the Legal Operations Manager may approve editorial changes. 5. Engineering publishes through Contentful after release testing. 6. IronVault stores the final version, approval record, translation evidence, and publication timestamp. Material changes must be communicated with reasonable advance notice where required. The prior version must remain retrievable for the applicable retention period. Discounts & Promotions Policy Owning area: Sales Last reviewed: August 2026 Policy ID: SAL-POL-014 Effective date: 1 September 2026 Policy owner: Director of Commercial Operations 1. Purpose and Overview This policy defines how IronStore plans, approves, launches, monitors, and closes discounts and promotional campaigns across its European e-commerce operations. It applies to customer-facing price reductions, voucher codes, bundles, free-gift offers, loyalty incentives, seasonal events, and marketplace promotions. The policy is intended to support consistent commercial decisions while protecting margin, pricing accuracy, customer trust, and compliance with applicable European consumer and advertising requirements. No promotion may be published unless its commercial terms, funding source, customer eligibility, and end date are documented and approved. 2. Scope This policy applies to:  IronStore websites, mobile applications, email, push notifications, affiliates, and social channels.  Promotions operated in EU and EEA markets, including EUR, GBP, SEK, DKK, PLN, and CZK price displays.  Products sold directly by IronStore and approved marketplace listings.  Supplier-funded, IronStore-funded, and jointly funded promotional activity.  Public offers and restricted offers for loyalty members, employees, customer service recovery, or selected segments. This policy does not replace:  Country-specific legal review for price reduction announcements.  The Pricing and Markdown Standard (COM-STD-006).  The Customer Voucher Terms published on each applicable storefront.  Marketplace-specific promotional rules. 3. Policy Statement IronStore promotions must be transparent, financially justified, technically controlled, and available on the terms communicated to customers. The advertised discount must be genuine, calculable, and supported by an approved reference price

applicable storefront.  Marketplace-specific promotional rules. 3. Policy Statement IronStore promotions must be transparent, financially justified, technically controlled, and available on the terms communicated to customers. The advertised discount must be genuine, calculable, and supported by an approved reference price or promotional mechanism.

Promotions must not:  Mislead customers about the size, duration, or availability of an offer.  Be configured to apply to products, countries, channels, or customers outside the approved scope.  Reduce the selling price below an approved minimum margin without written exception approval.  Use a reference price that has not been validated under the applicable country rules.  Be extended or relaunched solely to create artificial urgency. The standard promotion record is the source of truth. It must be maintained in PromoHub, with links to the campaign brief, approval record, pricing validation, creative assets, and post-campaign results. 4. Promotion Planning and Approval 4.1 Campaign brief The requesting team must create a PromoHub record at least:  10 business days before launch for standard promotions.  15 business days before launch for multi-country campaigns.  3 business days before launch for an operational or customer-service recovery offer. The brief must include:  Campaign name, objective, owner, markets, channels, and customer segment.  Start and end date, including time zone and any early-termination rule.  SKU or category scope, stock assumptions, exclusions, and expected units.  Discount type, funding split, expected revenue, gross margin, and budget.  Customer-facing terms, voucher limits, and required legal wording.  Tracking plan, reporting owner, and rollback procedure. 4.2 Approval thresholds Approval is based on the greater of the planned promotional cost or expected margin impact:  Up to €10,000: Category Manager and Commercial Finance Analyst.  €10,001–€50,000: Head of Sales and Finance Business Partner.

and rollback procedure. 4.2 Approval thresholds Approval is based on the greater of the planned promotional cost or expected margin impact:  Up to €10,000: Category Manager and Commercial Finance Analyst.  €10,001–€50,000: Head of Sales and Finance Business Partner.  €50,001–€150,000: Commercial Director and Finance Director.  Above €150,000: Chief Commercial Officer and CFO.  Any campaign below the approved minimum margin: Commercial Director and Finance Director, regardless of value. Non-standard terms require additional review:

 Legal review for price claims, “lowest price,” “last chance,” comparative advertising, or country-specific restrictions.  Data Protection review where customer segmentation uses sensitive or restricted data.  Marketplace Operations approval for third-party marketplace campaigns.  Tax review where the offer changes VAT treatment, invoicing, or cross-border settlement. Approvals must be recorded in PromoHub or the linked ServiceNow request. Email approval alone is not sufficient unless attached to the campaign record. 5. Discount and Promotion Rules 5.1 Percentage and fixed-price discounts  The discount must be calculated from the approved base price in the PriceGrid system.  The base price, promotional price, currency, and validity period must be consistent across the storefront and campaign creative.  Rounding follows the local currency rules configured in PriceGrid.  “Up to” claims must identify the applicable product range and must not imply that all products receive the maximum reduction.  Product exclusions must be visible before checkout, not only in full terms. For price-reduction communications, the responsible country team must validate the reference-price period required in that market. The validated reference price and evidence must be stored with the campaign record. 5.2 Voucher codes Voucher codes must be generated and controlled in VoucherAdmin. Required controls include:  Unique code or approved reusable code with a defined audience.  Start and expiry timestamp in Central European Time unless otherwise stated.  Maximum redemptions, customer limit, and order limit.  Eligible markets, channels, products, and minimum basket value.  Treatment of delivery charges, gift cards,

with a defined audience.  Start and expiry timestamp in Central European Time unless otherwise stated.  Maximum redemptions, customer limit, and order limit.  Eligible markets, channels, products, and minimum basket value.  Treatment of delivery charges, gift cards, and already discounted products.  Fraud controls, including code sharing and automated redemption monitoring. Unless the campaign brief states otherwise, vouchers cannot be combined with another percentage discount, employee discount, or compensation credit. Customer service may issue a one-time recovery voucher up to €25 without Sales approval, provided the reason is logged in Zendesk. 5.3 Bundles, multi-buy offers, and free gifts Bundle pricing must show:

 The products included.  The total price or saving.  Any mandatory quantity or mix requirement.  Whether substitutions are permitted.  The availability condition for a free gift. The free-gift SKU must be reserved in StockPilot before launch. If the gift becomes unavailable, the campaign must be paused or the approved substitute must be supplied. Checkout must not charge for a free gift unless the terms clearly explain a refundable deposit or similar mechanism. Multi-buy discounts must be tested for partial quantities, returns, cancellations, and split shipments. The system must apply the discount consistently and show the allocation on the order confirmation. 5.4 Loyalty, employee, and targeted promotions Targeted promotions must use approved audiences in Customer360 and comply with applicable consent and opt-out settings.  Loyalty offers must state membership eligibility and any points impact.  Employee discounts may be used only by verified employees and approved household members.  Employee discounts must not be combined with public promotions unless explicitly approved.  Personalised offers must not use protected characteristics or restricted profiling attributes.  Campaign files containing customer-level data must not be exported to unapproved tools. 6. Launch Controls and Monitoring The Campaign Operations Specialist owns the pre-launch checklist. Testing must be completed in the relevant storefront, currency, device types, and payment flows. currency, device types, and payment flows. At minimum, testing must verify:  Correct product eligibility and exclusion logic.  Correct displayed price, basket calculation, and tax treatment.  Voucher acceptance, rejection, expiry, and redemption limits.  Mobile and desktop creative, landing pages, and legal terms.  Order confirmation, invoice, refund, and return calculations.  Stock, delivery promise, and free-gift allocation. A second person must complete the checklist for campaigns with an expected daily revenue above €25,000. Monitoring is daily for major campaigns and at least every two business days for standard campaigns. The owner must pause a promotion and notify Commercial Operations if:  The discount applies outside the approved scope.  Margin is more than 3 percentage points below forecast.  A technical defect creates an unintended price.  Fraud or automated code use exceeds the agreed threshold.  Stock or fulfilment capacity cannot support the advertised offer. Material customer-impacting errors must be escalated through the Incident Management Standard (OPS-STD-009). Customer remediation is coordinated by Customer Experience and approved by Sales Operations. 7. Campaign Closure and Reporting The campaign owner must close the promotion at the approved end time and confirm that cached pages, feeds, ads, and scheduled messages have been removed or updated. A campaign may be extended only through a recorded approval; the original end date must not be altered retrospectively. Sales Commission Plan Owning area: Sales Last reviewed: August 2026 Policy ID: SAL-CMP-004 Effective date: 1 September 2026 Document owner: Director of Sales Operations Purpose and Overview This plan defines how IronStore sales employees earn variable commission for profitable, compliant revenue generation. It applies to sales activity across IronStore’s European e-commerce operations, including consumer electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty products, and other approved categories. The plan is designed to reward sustainable sales rather than order volume alone. Commission is based on eligible net revenue, contribution margin, customer quality, and achievement against approved targets. Payments are subject to order validation, returns processing, fraud controls, and payroll requirements. The plan is reviewed annually by Sales Operations, Finance, People, and Legal. The Director of Sales must approve any exception before it is communicated to an employee. Scope This plan applies to:  Account Executives, Sales Specialists, and approved Marketplace Sales Managers.  Employees assigned an individual or team sales target in Workday.  Permanent employees and fixed-term employees whose contracts expressly include variable pay.  Sales generated in approved European markets and recorded in the assigned Salesforce opportunity or channel account. This plan does not apply to:  Customer Service, warehouse, procurement, or affiliate employees unless separately covered by a written incentive plan.  Contractors, agency workers, interns, or employees on plans that expressly replace this plan.  Orders generated solely through paid media, automated campaigns, or customer self-service without documented sales ownership.  Revenue from prohibited products, internal purchases, test

incentive plan.  Contractors, agency workers, interns, or employees on plans that expressly replace this plan.  Orders generated solely through paid media, automated campaigns, or customer self-service without documented sales ownership.  Revenue from prohibited products, internal purchases, test orders, fraudulent transactions, or policy violations. Policy Statement

Commission is earned only when an eligible order meets all validation requirements. A booked order is not automatically commissionable. Revenue must be attributable to the employee, accepted by the customer, and not excluded under this plan. IronStore may correct, defer, reduce, or recover commission where an order is returned, cancelled, refunded, unpaid, incorrectly attributed, or found to breach commercial or compliance rules. Changes are applied in the next practical payroll cycle and are documented in the Commission Management Portal. No employee may offer unapproved discounts, alter customer ownership, split orders, or delay cancellations to influence commission. Suspected manipulation is handled under the Sales Conduct Standard and may result in disciplinary action. Commission Structure Target and On-Target Earnings Each eligible employee receives the following information in Workday before the start of the plan year:  Annual sales target.  Target commission amount.  Commission period and currency.  Individual or team weighting.  Applicable product-category modifiers.  Threshold, accelerator, and maximum rules. The standard plan year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Employees joining or leaving during the year receive a prorated target based on active employment days, subject to their employment contract and local law. Unless otherwise stated:  70% of commission is based on individual eligible net revenue.  30% is based on the assigned team target.  Employees with no individual portfolio use a 100% team-based measure.  Targets are adjusted only for approved transfers, extended leave, territory changes, or material business restructuring. Eligible Net Revenue Eligible

 30% is based on the assigned team target.  Employees with no individual portfolio use a 100% team-based measure.  Targets are adjusted only for approved transfers, extended leave, territory changes, or material business restructuring. Eligible Net Revenue Eligible net revenue is calculated as: Customer invoice value excluding VAT, delivery charges, gift cards, refunds, cancellations, credits, and non-commissionable fees. Revenue is credited to the employee who is recorded as the primary owner in Salesforce at the time the order is accepted in the Order Management System (OMS). Split credit requires approval from the Sales Manager and Sales Operations before month-end close.

The following are excluded:  Orders below the approved minimum margin.  Employee, test, or related-party purchases.  Orders later identified as fraudulent or sanctioned-party transactions.  Free replacements, warranty fulfilment, and goodwill orders.  Revenue generated by an unapproved reseller or marketplace channel.  Orders where the employee did not perform a documented sales activity. Margin and Category Modifiers Commission is calculated using the standard category rate table maintained by Finance. The current default rates are:  Standard categories: 1.0% of eligible net revenue.  Strategic or high-margin categories: 1.25%.  Low-margin or clearance categories: 0.50%.  Approved new-market launches: 1.50% for the first 90 days, subject to Finance approval. A category modifier applies based on the product classification in the Product Information Management system (PIM), not the description used in a sales proposal. Finance may update category rates quarterly with at least 30 days’ notice. Orders with contribution margin below 8% are non-commissionable unless the Commercial Director approves the transaction in writing before order acceptance. Margin exceptions must include the customer, SKU group, expected revenue, and commercial rationale. Calculation and Achievement Monthly Calculation Sales Operations calculates preliminary commission after monthly close using data from:  Salesforce for ownership and opportunity history.  OMS for order status and fulfilment.  Snowflake Finance Mart for revenue and margin.  NetSuite for refunds, credits, and payment status. The monthly calculation is normally completed by the eighth working day of the following month. Employees receive a statement in the Commission Management Portal

 Snowflake Finance Mart for revenue and margin.  NetSuite for refunds, credits, and payment status. The monthly calculation is normally completed by the eighth working day of the following month. Employees receive a statement in the Commission Management Portal showing:  Target and achievement percentage.  Eligible revenue by category.  Applied rates and modifiers.

 Returns, credits, or other deductions.  Preliminary commission and any prior-period adjustments. Quota Attainment The standard attainment curve is:  Below 70% of target: no commission on the affected measure.  70% to 99.99%: commission paid at the applicable base rate.  100% to 119.99%: 1.25x accelerator on revenue above 100%.  120% to 149.99%: 1.50x accelerator on revenue above 120%.  150% and above: 2.00x accelerator on revenue above 150%. Accelerators apply only after the relevant threshold is reached and do not retroactively increase commission on earlier revenue. Total annual commission is capped at 200% of target commission unless the Chief Commercial Officer approves an exception. Team commission is calculated against the approved team target. Team attainment is based on aggregated eligible revenue after all returns, exclusions, and margin adjustments. New Starters, Transfers, and Leave  New starters begin earning from their approved start date and system assignment date.  Employees transferring teams retain credit for accepted orders owned before the transfer.  Open opportunities transfer only when approved in Salesforce by both managers.  Extended statutory leave is handled according to local law and the employee’s contract.  Temporary cover does not automatically receive commission credit; a written split arrangement is required. Order Validation, Returns, and Clawbacks Commission is normally paid after the order has passed the applicable validation period. For recurring or high-value orders, Finance may hold payment until customer payment is received. The following adjustments apply:  Cancelled orders are removed in the month of

Commission is normally paid after the order has passed the applicable validation period. For recurring or high-value orders, Finance may hold payment until customer payment is received. The following adjustments apply:  Cancelled orders are removed in the month of cancellation.  Full refunds reverse 100% of the related commission.  Partial refunds reverse commission proportionately.  Returns are adjusted after the standard 30-day return window, or later if the product category has a longer statutory or contractual period.  Chargebacks and confirmed fraud are fully reversed.  Bad debt may be reversed after Finance classifies the invoice as impaired.

If a negative adjustment exceeds the current month’s commission, the balance is carried forward for up to six months. IronStore will not make deductions from salary except where legally permitted and properly authorised. Any recovery must comply with local employment and payroll rules. Payment and Disputes Approved commission is paid through monthly payroll, normally in the second payroll following the relevant month. Payment is made in the employee’s payroll currency and is subject to tax, social security, and other statutory deductions. Employees must review their statement within 10 calendar days. Disputes must be submitted through the Commission Management Portal using the “Commission Review” form and include:  Order or opportunity number.  Reason for disagreement.  Supporting customer or system evidence.  Requested correction. Sales Operations acknowledges submissions within three working days and normally completes the review within 10 working days. Disputes involving ownership, margin exceptions, or policy interpretation are escalated to the Director of Sales Operations and Finance Business Partner. Unresolved disputes may be referred to People Operations. Roles and Responsibilities  Sales employee: Maintain accurate opportunities, follow pricing rules, and review monthly statements.  Sales Manager: Set targets, approve ownership changes, validate exceptions, and monitor conduct.  Sales Operations: Maintain the plan, calculate commission, administer disputes, and publish statements.  Finance: Own rate tables, validate revenue and margin, process adjustments, and approve exceptions.  People Operations: Confirm employment status, contract terms, payroll treatment, and local-law requirements.  Legal and Compliance: Advise on regulatory, anti-bribery, competition, and customer-protection matters.

statements.  Finance: Own rate tables, validate revenue and margin, process adjustments, and approve exceptions.  People Operations: Confirm employment status, contract terms, payroll treatment, and local-law requirements.  Legal and Compliance: Advise on regulatory, anti-bribery, competition, and customer-protection matters.  Director of Sales: Approve material policy exceptions and annual plan changes.  Chief Commercial Officer: Approve commission caps or exceptions above delegated authority. Sales Playbook Owning area: Sales Last reviewed: August 2026 Document owner: Director of Sales Operations Policy reference: SAL-PLB-001 Applies to: IronStore commercial teams in the European Economic Area and United Kingdom 1. Purpose and Overview This playbook defines the standard sales approach for IronStore’s consumer-product business. It provides a common operating model for acquiring, qualifying, converting, and retaining customers across electronics, home essentials, clothing, outdoor equipment, beauty, and related categories. IronStore primarily serves consumers through its online storefronts and mobile channels. Sales activity must support profitable growth, accurate customer communication, compliant data handling, and a consistent customer experience across markets. The playbook applies to direct sales activity, marketplace opportunities, affiliate partnerships, business-to-business enquiries, and promotional campaigns managed by Sales or in partnership with Marketing, Merchandising, and Customer Operations. 2. Scope This document covers:  Customer and opportunity qualification.  Sales pipeline management in Salesforce.  Pricing, promotions, discounts, and commercial approvals.  Sales handover to Customer Operations, Finance, and Fulfilment.  Key account and partner management.  Performance reporting and required sales hygiene.  Escalation of legal, financial, reputational, or customer-risk issues. This playbook does not replace:  Country-specific consumer protection or VAT requirements.  The Privacy and Data Handling Standard (LEG-PRV-002).  Product safety, restricted goods, or marketplace operating procedures.  Employment policies or compensation plans.

4.2 Qualification The assigned representative must make an initial qualification attempt within:  Four business hours for high-value partner or business enquiries.  One business day for standard inbound enquiries.  Two business days for campaign-generated leads. Use the BANT-E framework:  Business need: What product, category, or commercial problem is being addressed?  Authority: Is the contact authorised to purchase or approve the proposal?  Need date: When is delivery or campaign activation required?  Timing and budget: Is there an approved budget or credible buying timeframe?  Evidence: What information confirms the opportunity is genuine? A qualified opportunity must include:  Customer or partner profile.  Estimated order value and currency.  Expected close date.  Product category and quantity, if known.  Delivery market and fulfilment constraints.  Decision-maker and next step.  Qualification notes supported by customer communication. Close or recycle a lead when it is duplicate, outside IronStore’s operating markets, commercially unviable, or unresponsive after three documented attempts over ten business days. 4.3 Opportunity Stages Salesforce opportunities use the following stages: 1. New: Lead accepted and ownership confirmed. 2. Qualified: Need, contact, market, and potential value recorded. 3. Solution agreed: Products, availability, delivery approach, and commercial terms discussed. 4. Proposal sent: Written quote or partner proposal issued. 5. Commit: Customer has confirmed intent, subject only to documented final conditions. 6. Closed won/lost: Order or agreement completed, or a reason for loss recorded. Each opportunity must contain a current next action. Opportunities without a completed activity

A quote may not be marked Commit based only on verbal optimism. Evidence must include a purchase order, signed agreement, confirmed checkout path, or written customer commitment. 4.4 Proposals and Quotes All commercial quotes must be generated from Salesforce CPQ or an approved country template. The quote must state:  Product description, SKU, quantity, and availability status.  Unit and total prices, currency, VAT treatment, and applicable fees.  Delivery estimate and delivery location.  Payment terms and quote expiry date.  Return, warranty, and cancellation conditions where relevant.  Named IronStore contact and escalation route. Standard quote validity is 14 calendar days unless stock, supplier pricing, or campaign terms require a shorter period. Sales representatives must not promise guaranteed delivery dates unless confirmed by the Order Management System (OMS) and the relevant fulfilment team. “Available to order” must not be described as “in stock.” 4.5 Discount and Margin Controls Discounts must protect the minimum contribution margin defined in the Commercial Margin Matrix (FIN-COM-004). Approval requirements:  Up to 5%: Sales representative, if within published campaign rules.  Above 5% and up to 10%: Regional Sales Manager.  Above 10%, below floor margin, or with free delivery outside campaign rules: Director of Sales and Finance Business Partner.  Any non-standard payment term, rebate, exclusivity, price guarantee, or marketing contribution: Commercial Director and Finance.  Any commitment exceeding €50,000 in gross order value: Director of Sales plus Finance approval.  Commitments exceeding €250,000, exclusivity, or contractual liability require Executive Commercial Committee

Approvals must be attached to the Salesforce opportunity before the quote is sent. Backdated or undocumented discounts are prohibited. Sales staff must not stack promotions unless the campaign rules explicitly permit it. Promotional codes intended for consumers must not be manually applied to business or partner orders without Commercial approval. 4.6 Order Handover

After customer acceptance, the sales owner must complete the Sales-to-Operations Handover in Salesforce within one business day. The handover must include:  Final quote or order reference.  Confirmed SKUs, quantities, prices, VAT, and delivery address.  Customer billing and contact details.  Payment status or approved payment terms.  Delivery deadline and any agreed service level.  Open risks, substitutions, or customer dependencies.  Relevant approval records and customer correspondence. Operations validates the order in the OMS. Sales must not confirm final fulfilment until Operations accepts the handover. If an order is delayed, partially unavailable, or materially different from the agreed terms, the sales owner must contact the customer within one business day of notification and document the resolution. 4.7 Account and Partner Management Strategic accounts and partners are reviewed according to tier:  Tier 1: More than €500,000 annual value or material strategic dependency; monthly review.  Tier 2: €100,000–€499,999 annual value; quarterly review.  Tier 3: Below €100,000 annual value; standard service and annual review. Account plans must include:  Revenue, margin, and order-frequency trends.  Product categories and growth opportunities.  Service issues, returns, and payment risks.  Contract dates and renewal actions.  Named stakeholders and relationship status.  A documented plan for the next 90 days. Partners must be assessed for brand, product compliance, data protection, payment, and reputational risk before onboarding. Regional managers review:  Pipeline coverage against monthly target.

 Stage ageing and stalled opportunities.  Commit accuracy.  Expected gross margin.  Risks involving stock, delivery, payment, or approval.  Lost opportunities and corrective actions. The standard planning assumption is 3x pipeline coverage against the remaining target, unless a regional plan specifies otherwise. Forecast categories:  Commit: High confidence; documented customer commitment.  Best case: Credible opportunity with unresolved conditions.  Pipeline: Qualified but not sufficiently advanced for the current forecast period.  Omitted: Not expected to close in the forecast period. Forecast manipulation, duplicate opportunities, inflated values, and artificial stage advancement are prohibited. Corrections must be made before the weekly review. 5. Customer Communication and Conduct Sales representatives must:  Use approved IronStore email signatures and country-language templates.  Identify IronStore clearly in outbound communications.  Honour unsubscribe and do-not-contact requests immediately.  Avoid claims about product performance, sustainability, availability, or savings unless supported by approved product or campaign information.  Use the customer’s preferred language where reasonably possible.  Record material commitments in Salesforce. Do not request or retain full payment-card details, account passwords, government identification, or unnecessary health information. Direct payment issues to the secure checkout or Finance process. Potential fraud indicators include mismatched billing and delivery details, unusual urgency, repeated failed payments, requests to redirect goods, or pressure to bypass standard approval. Escalate suspected fraud to Fraud Operations and do not accuse the customer or continue informal negotiation. 6. Page 28 — Product Administration Notes Size and fit conventions IronStore uses EU sizing for most apparel. Where a supplier uses inch-based measurements, the product record includes waist and inseam values. Fit descriptions are standardized as follows:  Slim fit: Close to the body with limited ease  Regular fit: Standard ease through chest, waist, or hip  Relaxed fit: Additional ease for comfort and layering  Oversized fit: Deliberately broader proportions and longer or dropped construction  Compression fit: Close-fitting technical garment intended to provide support Customers should be directed to the product-specific size chart when available. Size charts are maintained separately from this catalog and may vary between product families. Care-label handling Care instructions in this catalog are the minimum operational guidance recorded for product listing and returns processing. The sewn-in care label takes precedence if there is a discrepancy. Products marked dry clean only must not be described as machine washable in customer-facing content. Underlay guidance

Underlay is recommended for most loose rugs on laminate, tile, polished wood, vinyl, and other smooth floors. Underlay improves stability and can reduce wear caused by repeated movement. For hand-knotted, handwoven, high-pile, and natural-fibre rugs, a breathable underlay is preferred. Returns and storage Rugs must be stored dry and protected from direct sunlight. Rolled products should remain on a suitable core where possible. Folded storage can result in permanent crease lines, especially in latex-backed or high-pile products. Natural-fibre rugs must not be stored in unventilated plastic wrapping. End of catalog.
